In four USDC-WETH pools benchmarked against Binance ETH-USDT from June to August 2026, the one-second benchmark innovation is sharply non-Gaussian: 73% of seconds show no price change. Cutting cadence from twelve seconds to one sheds 84.5% of the expected shock, so a twelve-second maker must screen at least 84.5% of informed flow to match a one-second venue, far above the 71.1% that a Gaussian model implies. In trending markets, the stale pool is picked off at execution: with-trend fills obtain an effective spread 11.1 bps lower than against-trend fills, with the same sign in all four pools.

papers.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
papers.abstract: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $β$ of $L(s,χ)$, for a primitive real character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-β)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,χ)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $β$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.

papers.title: ProV-Mem: Proactive Memory for Streaming Video Question Answering
papers.abstract: Proactive streaming video question answering requires a model to continuously monitor an incoming stream and autonomously decide when to speak, what to say, and whether to emit a response. Existing streaming systems face a fundamental difficulty: retaining long visual histories is costly, whereas discarding them can lead to missed events and repeated responses. We propose \textbf{ProV-Mem}, a training-free proactive memory framework built around a frozen VLM backbone. ProV-Mem decomposes the proactive decision into three lightweight memory tiers: a temporal-trigger memory controls when to query the backbone and recovers from prolonged silence, an instructional memory guides what to say through a fixed prompting prior for concise and visually grounded generation, and an episodic memory determines whether to emit by filtering near-duplicate responses. Under an idealized conditional-sufficiency assumption, we derive a stagewise approximation bound relating the decomposed process to a full-state joint policy. We further introduce Cost-Aware Area Under the Curve (\textbf{CAUC}), which extends PAUC by explicitly discounting redundant, overly frequent, and unnecessarily long emissions. Experiments on the four scenarios of ProactiveVideoQA show that ProV-Mem achieves the best CAUC across all scenarios and the best PAUC on WEB, EGO, and TV, while maintaining low per-response inference latency.

papers.title: QREF: Improving DeepSearch Agents by Aligning Search with Reasoning via Query Refinement and Evidence Filtering
papers.abstract: DeepSearch agents achieve strong performance on complex information-seeking tasks through iterative search and reasoning. However, they often issue intent-misaligned, under-constrained, or redundant search queries, resulting in poor evidence coverage and accumulating retrieval noise. To mitigate these limitations, we propose QREF, a plug-and-play Query Refiner and Evidence Filter. Specifically, the Query Refiner rewrites search queries according to the current reasoning intent while ensuring complementary coverage across each search batch. The Evidence Filter retains evidence relevant to both the current search batch and the reasoning objective, reducing distracting retrieval results. We initialize the Query Refiner with supervised fine-tuning and optimize it through reinforcement learning based on interactions with a real-world web search environment, reducing ineffective queries. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our approach improves the performance of DeepSearch agents across four challenging benchmarks, achieving average relative Pass@1 improvements of 33.55% on WebSailor and 11.04% on TongyiDeepResearch without modifying architectures or retraining their reasoning policies. Compared with the original DeepSearch backbone without QREF, the RL-trained refiner reduces the fraction of query batches that lack discriminative retrieval anchors by 95%. Compared with the SFT-trained refiner, it also lowers the filter-based ineffective query ratio.

papers.title: Probing cold gas and dust in quiescent galaxies across cosmic time
papers.abstract: The discovery of massive quiescent galaxies at high redshift by JWST has revealed that star formation can cease rapidly in the early Universe, yet the physical mechanisms responsible for quenching remain unknown. A key missing element is the systematic measurement in statistically representative quiescent samples of the cold gas and dust content, which are crucial for distinguishing quenching mechanisms and evolutionary pathways. Such observations are currently not feasible because state-of-the-art sub-millimeter facilities (e.g., ALMA) cannot routinely detect the faint molecular gas and dust reservoirs of quiescent galaxies, nor pinpoint outflowing molecular gas. A next-generation facility (ALMA2040) capable of providing transformative access to the cold interstellar medium of quiescent galaxies across redshift is therefore essential. In particular, it will allow the community to probe the molecular gas content of quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon and beyond by targeting the CO, [CI], and [CII] emission lines, as well as unveiling the physical conditions of the cold interstellar medium by constraining the CO spectral line energy distribution. It will also reveal the dust content of the passive population, a crucial ingredient to constrain the different quenching mechanisms. Finally, it will enable probing the molecular gas kinematics and identify molecular outflows driven by supermassive black holes. When combined with the rich legacy of JWST, ELT, and SKAO surveys, ALMA2040 will deliver a comprehensive, multi-phase view of feedback and quenching, allowing us to establish when, how, and why galaxies shut down their star formation across cosmic time.

papers.title: Poison Valleys: Diagnosing Path-Dependent Failure in LLM Code Repair
papers.abstract: When code-repair agents fail, final tests reveal that a patch is wrong but not which earlier commitment caused it or which software obligation failed. Poison Valleys traces this path in 1,844 model requests on two synthetic Python cases: PersistQueue adds atomic batch claiming to a disk-backed queue, while Dijkstra adds source-sensitive filtering to shortest-path search. We define plausible but incorrect software mechanisms, place each in a model's hypothesis, implementation plan, or both, and evaluate the generated code with an Oracle and targeted diagnostic coordinates. Moving the misconception from hypothesis to plan increased failure by 32.2% in PersistQueue and 28.9% in Dijkstra after matching the experimental mix. Different misconceptions produced distinct, model-dependent patterns of violated obligations, although several could converge on the same behavior. This creates a measured connection from upstream misconception to code mechanism and failure form. Code, data, and demo: https://poisonvalleys.org.

papers.title: TRACE: Typed Reference-Aware Conversational Editing for Humanoid Motion Diffusion
papers.abstract: Language-conditioned humanoid motion generation enables users to create and refine robot movements through natural language. The central challenge is to connect an underspecified request to concrete motion structure that can subsequently be revised relative to an accepted reference. We present TRACE, a generation and editing framework for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot built around typed, measurable kinematic quantities. Our insight is to ground generation conditions in paired training motions and editing goals in the current motion. A language model learns to predict support, root, and hand events from motion-derived supervision; their time-aligned encodings complement the original text in a diffusion generator. Gravity-referenced states and trajectory--contact objectives improve kinematic consistency. For editing, typed requests define body--time scopes and source-relative goals. A separate reference-conditioned diffusion editor uses these goals and revised events to realize changes, while sampling-time projection preserves protected state coordinates. Quantitative evaluation and human assessment show improved semantic alignment and motion quality over the compared methods. Multi-turn editing evaluations demonstrate more reliable execution of successive relative requests under shared preservation constraints. Code is available at https://github.com/Multimodal-Perception-Action/TRACE.

papers.title: Algorithms for computing basins of attraction associated with a rational self-map of the Hopf fibration based on Lyapunov exponents
papers.abstract: The objective of this work is twofold. One, we develop a theory of iteration for complex rational functions so that the problems of overflow and indeterminacy caused by null, or almost null, denominators can be avoided when developing implementations. Second, we present easily implementable methods that allow the calculation of attracting cycles as well as the graphical representation of their basins of attraction. In order to deal with our first goal, we work with homogeneous complex coordinates, and we take the complex projective line as a model, which is expressed as a quotient of the 3-sphere through the Hopf fibration. An irreducible representation of a rational function can now be presented as a Hopf fibration endomorphism. As well as our second goal is concerned, we use Lyapunov functions and exponents to calculate the cycles associated with endomorphisms and to graphically represent the corresponding basins of attraction. We point out that our algorithms are based on the calculation of a finite set of non-negative real constants, and their calculation does not depend on the previous determination of the fixed points or attracting cycles.

papers.title: Space Sustainability: The Global Commons
papers.abstract: Space is no longer a distant, barely reachable frontier of scientific exploration; it has become a critical infrastructure for life on Earth and a rapidly expanding zone of intense commercial activity. Yet this expansion is unfolding in ways that replicate, and amplify, the unsustainable dynamics already driving ecological and social crises on our planet. This chapter explains the concept of space sustainability as a multidimensional challenge; it raises the questions of governance, knowledge, power, justice, and global responsibility. It highlights both the profound benefits derived from space activities and the uneven distribution of costs and risks, from orbital debris and atmospheric impacts to privatization of essential services. We therefore argue that it frames space as a global commons that demands stewardship rather than pure exploitation, cooperation rather than competition, and governance that prioritizes long-term wellbeing rather than laissez-faire approach. Sustainability in space is inseparable from sustainability on Earth. This chapter invites readers, whether they are space administration and industry actors, policymakers, scientists, or simply engaged citizens, to see space not as a limitless frontier, but as a shared domain whose future depends on collective choices made today.

papers.title: SCRIBE: Scalable Contextual Representations of Interpretable Brain-Grounded Semantics
papers.abstract: Understanding how the human brain constructs meaning from real-world language remains a fundamental challenge, as semantics depend on context that varies in natural settings. To enable the study of real-world linguistic meaning in the brain, we introduce SCRIBE, a framework grounded in a neuroscience-informed semantic space that leverages an ensemble of open-source large language models to generate interpretable, word-level semantic representations of arbitrary text. In a behavioral study with 921 participants, we show that human semantic feature judgments vary systematically with context, and that SCRIBE captures these shifts, reaching 75-81% of the estimated human noise ceiling. Using brain activity recorded while participants listen to naturalistic stories, we further demonstrate that SCRIBE predicts neural responses in language-selective brain regions, significantly outperforming non-contextual semantic representations. Variance partitioning reveals that SCRIBE explains unique brain-predictive information beyond syntactic features, suggesting that its representations capture aspects of linguistic meaning not accounted for by the measured syntactic features. Together, these findings establish SCRIBE as a scalable and interpretable foundation for studying natural language semantics in the brain.

papers.title: On micro-macro derivation of traffic flow models with $(A,B)$-connection and its stability
papers.abstract: We show that $(A,B)$-connections for conservations laws with a flux discontinuity can be obtained as limits of perturbed Follow-the-Leader (FtL) models, and provide continuity and surjectivity of the map associating the perturbation of the dynamics with the flux limiter.

papers.title: Hierarchical Interpretable Multitask Audio Representation Learning: An Analysis of Event-Scene Relationships through the Information Bottleneck
papers.abstract: Joint Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC) and Audio Tagging (AT) models traditionally rely on unconstrained multihead architectures. However, this design ignores the natural hierarchical dependency between sounds and acoustic scenes. In this work, we investigate a hierarchical (sequential) conditioning paradigm that predicts scene categories directly from intermediate event probabilities. Through a large-scale empirical benchmark with 66 full training runs across three state-of-the-art backbones (PaSST, PANNs, and BEATs) and different loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.0, 1.0]), we show that hierarchical conditioning achieves competitive classification performance while altering multitask optimization dynamics. Unlike multihead baselines, which sequentially solve the easier ASC task before optimizing AT, the hierarchical architecture enables synchronized dual-task learning for specific loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.6, 0.9]). Furthermore, we propose a multi-perspective interpretability framework that combines an analysis of the information bottleneck, manifold geometry, and Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) on a Term-Frequency Inverse-Document-Frequency (TF-IDF) event representation, providing complementary insights into event-scene relationships. Our findings reveal that hierarchical conditioning systematically yields lower conditional entropy, higher mutual information, and superior latent cluster separability (higher Silhouette scores), establishing a more structured and semantically faithful intermediate feature space.

papers.title: Wavefront Engineering for Physical Layer Security in Near-Field Wireless Communications
papers.abstract: With wireless transmission exposing information to potential interception by unintended receivers, physical layer security (PLS) offers a promising approach to securing wireless communications. Beamforming can mitigate this vulnerability by exploiting the spatial characteristics of wireless propagation to concentrate power toward the intended receiver while suppressing it at potential eavesdroppers. However, as wireless systems enter the radiating near field of large-aperture antenna arrays, the resulting wavefront curvature provides additional opportunities for spatial wavefront engineering to enhance PLS. In this work, we investigate the use of different beam types for PLS, including focused, curved, abruptly autofocusing, and cosine beams, generated using uniform linear and planar arrays (ULAs/UPAs). To quantify their performance, we introduce power-based metrics that characterize the power received by the legitimate user and a potential eavesdropper. For all beam types we introduce focusing along the vertical UPA direction, to independently control the phase distributions along the two UPA dimensions and enhance the power discrimination between the legitimate receiver and the eavesdropper. We also propose hollow-focused beams, in which an inactive strip is introduced in the transmitting aperture to create a protected low-power region between the transmitter and the legitimate receiver. The results demonstrate that vertical focusing dramatically enhances the PLS performance and that hollow-focused beams achieve superior PLS performance in both line-of-sight (LoS) and vicinity-of-user (VoU) scenarios.

papers.title: BOLT: Multi-Bottleneck Bound-Guided Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling with Time Lags and Resource-Coupled Transport
papers.abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. The root bound certifies a completed schedule's suboptimality gap without a solver. On industry-motivated 10-module prefabricated-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%. Across five zero-shot 50- and 80-module production batches, BOLT outperforms the best dispatching-rule pair on four and the penalty policy on the three with long moves. In the three-vehicle 80-module batch, its mean makespan is 13.0% below the best pair and 4.2% below an hour-budget constraint-programming solver whose proven gap averages 34%. BOLT decides in 2.3-5.9 ms per event on one processor core and re-plans a disruption in seconds.

papers.title: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Specialized vision-language-action (VLA) policies acquire strong domain-specific skills, yet consolidating these skills into one shared policy remains challenging. On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher knowledge on inputs induced by the student, addressing the distribution mismatch encountered during deployment. For flow-based VLAs, this mismatch arises at two levels: environment observations and intermediate action-generation states. We propose a two-level on-policy distillation framework that couples student-driven environment interaction with teacher velocity supervision along student-generated action flow trajectories. Frozen domain specialists jointly supervise one student. After each update, the student collects new environment experience and generates fresh action-flow trajectories. Starting from a joint supervised fine-tuning (SFT) initialization, Velocity Loss OPD yields absolute success-rate gains of 22.55% on LIBERO-40, 33.4% on CALVIN five-instruction sequences, and 22.6% on Meta-World MT50. Compared with Action Loss OPD and Teacher-rollout SFT, it achieves absolute success-rate gains of 6.4-9.5% on LIBERO-40, 9.7-18.3% on CALVIN, and 3.2-4.2% on Meta-World MT50. Analysis by sequence length further shows larger success-rate gains on longer CALVIN sequences. These results demonstrate effective multi-domain capability consolidation through two-level on-policy supervision, with a single student deployed across domains.

papers.title: Non-equilibrium Muon Dynamics Imitating Fractional Spin Excitations in a Quantum Spin Chain
papers.abstract: Fractional spin excitations in low-dimensional and frustrated magnets are commonly associated with sporadic spin fluctuations, as observed in quantum spin liquids, spin ices, and other complex magnetic states. In this study, we investigate the spin dynamics in the amplitude-modulated magnetic ground state of AgCuVO$_4$, a spin-1/2 chain compound with competing intrachain interactions, by muon spectroscopy. Our data reveal a Gaussian decay of muon polarization that remains remarkably resilient against applied magnetic fields---a behavior often interpreted as evidence of emergent sporadic spin dynamics. However, density functional theory calculations of muon stopping sites and their quadrupolar level-crossing resonance spectra suggest an alternative mechanism: a two-state model where the muon randomly hops between two nearby sites, eventually equilibrating across both on a microsecond timescale via quantum delocalization. These findings provide a microscopic explanation for the field-resilient muon polarization and indicate that such behavior may not always stem from intrinsic spin fluctuations, but can also arise from non-equilibrium muon dynamics.

papers.title: Direct measures of black hole masses through cosmic time
papers.abstract: Supermassive black holes (BHs) are thought to reside in all massive galaxies. They play a fundamental role in shaping galaxy evolution by suppressing star formation and halting the stellar growth of the most massive galaxies via feedback mechanisms. However, to date, measuring even their most basic property, their mass, is still challenging. The mass of BHs carries information on the growth history and the mutual interplay with the host galaxy. Uncertain BH masses leave many key questions on galaxy evolution wide open. Here we show that a transformational facility such as ALMA2040 would open a new window to measure BH mass by directly observing the kinematics of cold gas in galaxy cores from the local Universe up to very high redshift, irrespective of BH activity. This would revolutionise our understanding of BH formation, growth, and their role within galaxy evolution.

papers.title: CriticaLLM: Using LLMs as Autonomous Game Master for Tabletop Role-Playing Games
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive capabilities across many tasks, including processing large amounts of text, following instructions, and generating ideas. This allows the use of such models in various contexts, including games and Tabletop Role-Playing Games (TTRPGs), such as Dungeons & Dragons. However, these games include many complex components, from crafting interesting stories to adhering to rules, while allowing some freedom in players' actions. In this work, we first highlight key components that LLMs should exhibit in the context of TTRPGs. Then, we introduce our framework, CriticaLLM, a fully automated Game Master that can run entire TTRPG games, from creating diverse and interesting stories to managing exploration and combat phases. We evaluate our framework with actual TTRPG players and examine the diversity of generated plots and antagonists across four LLMs of varying sizes. Overall, our framework appears to be a promising option for running entire TTRPG games.

papers.title: On the Robustness of Gossip Protocols in Modern Blockchains
papers.abstract: Modern platforms such as Ethereum and Polkadot nowadays execute Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus protocols over large validator committees, often comprising hundreds of nodes. At this scale, complete graph topologies for connecting nodes are impractical, leading systems to adopt various gossip mechanisms, often in an ad hoc manner. In this paper, we study the robustness of widely deployed gossip protocols used in committee-based blockchains against realistic network adversaries. We show, both analytically and through extensive empirical measurements, that the graph parameters commonly chosen to instantiate random graphs are insufficient to guarantee that enough honest nodes receive consensus messages for quorum formation in existing protocols. Motivated by this finding, we empirically assess the robustness of Bitcoin's Erdős-Rényi (ER) graphs, Polkadot's grid topology, Ethereum's GossipSub, and Solana's chunk- and tree-based disseminations. Our results reveal surprising tradeoffs: Solana's dynamic trees are bandwidth-efficient in benign settings but fragile under adaptive attacks; Polkadot's grid achieves strong robustness at the cost of high bandwidth overhead; GossipSub is both bandwidth-efficient and resilient to adaptive adversaries, yet highly sensitive to parameter choices; and ER graphs provide a strong robustness-efficiency tradeoff, e.g., when the (average) fanout degree exceeds 15 for networks up to 5000 nodes.

papers.title: Activation-Adjacent Layer Normalization: Effects on Approximation Power
papers.abstract: Layer normalization (LN) and root mean square normalization (RMSNorm) depend on their inputs and remain nonlinear at inference. Inserting either next to an activation may therefore change the function a network represents. We study when shallow activation-normalized (AN) and preactivation-normalized (PN) networks can approximate a prescribed width-$N$ one-hidden-layer MLP. Viewing RMSNorm as input-dependent scaling, we use width augmentation to locally linearize normalization on compact feature sets. For AN networks, an unbounded activation range allows width $N+1$, while every continuous nonconstant activation admits width $N+r$ with error $O_f(r^{-1})$. For PN networks, affine parameters or, without them, degree-one positive homogeneity recover width $N+1$; general continuous activations admit width $N+r$ with error tending to zero. The corresponding LN constructions use centered coordinate pairs, yielding widths $N+2$ and $N+2r$, respectively. We prove that $N+1$ for RMSNorm and $N+2$ for LN are also the worst-case bound for approximations, and show that applicable universal-approximation theorems for ordinary MLPs transfer to these normalized architectures. Numerical experiments recover the predicted approximation rates for both normalizations across all five settings and illustrate the shifted-ReLU finite-width obstruction.

papers.title: Quantum Cosmology in Page-Wootters' Framework: Singularity Resolution and Clock Coherence
papers.abstract: We investigate the fate of big-bang singularity and coherence between distinct clock states in a quantum cosmological setting within the Page-Wootters framework. With a canonically quantized plane-symmetric Bianchi I universe, we employ Dirac factorization of the Wheeler-DeWitt constraint and obtain a Schrodinger-like equation which is first-order in an internal clock variable. By constructing its solution as a Gaussian wave packet in the expanding branch, we derive the corresponding conditional state and probability density of the universe. We find that the conditional probability density vanishes in the zero-volume limit, indicating resolution of the big-bang singularity within this probabilistic framework. Another prespective of the study is provided by the construction of density matrix from the conditional states associated with different clock readings and the remaining degree of freedom. By tracing out the remaining subsystem, we obtain the reduced density matrix and analyze the resulting coherence as a function of separation between different clock states. These results provide a relational characterization of singularity resolution and demonstrate how the spectral properties of the quantum state govern the temporal coherence between different clock states in the Page-Wootters description.

papers.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.

papers.title: The Bardos-Tartar Conjecture for the Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible viscous Navier-Stokes equations in dimension $d=2,3$ with periodic boundary conditions and time-independent external forcing. When $d=2$, the Bardos-Tartar conjecture asks whether the set of solutions at any given positive time is dense in the Hilbert subspace of $L^2$ consisting of mean-zero divergence-free vector fields, with respect to the strong $L^2$ norm. We prove the Bardos-Tartar conjecture and, more generally, its analogue for the hyperviscous Navier-Stokes equations studied by Guo-Titi. In addition, for $d=2,3$ we show that any given initial condition is either backwards-extendable (i) for all values of viscosity $ν>0$, or (ii) only for viscosities that belong to a Lebesgue-null subset of $\mathbb{R}_+$. When (i) holds, we show the initial condition and forcing must be real-analytic (in fact, both belong to $D(e^{σA})$ for some $σ>0$, where $A$ is the Stokes operator). Furthermore, we show that (i) is extremely unstable under perturbations. In particular, given any initial condition we show that two Fourier modes can be perturbed so that (ii) holds.

papers.title: Incremental Exact Vertex Connectivity
papers.abstract: We study the problem of maintaining the vertex connectivity $κ$ of a graph under edge insertions. For undirected graphs, our algorithm uses $O(κ^4 \log^2 n)$ amortized time per edge insertion. After each edge insertion, the algorithm outputs the current value of $κ$, plus a set of $κ$ vertices whose removal disconnects the graph. Our algorithm is Monte-Carlo randomized and works with a randomness-adaptive adversary. The algorithm also works on directed graphs against an oblivious adversary, which is equivalent to an output-adaptive adversary if we only have to output the current value of $κ$. Previously, algorithms using SPQR trees could maintain the vertex connectivity in undirected graphs with $O(\log n)$ time per edge insertion for $κ\le 3$, but no algorithm with $o(n)$ time per edge insertion was known for $κ\ge 4$. Moreover, for $κ\ge 4$, on general directed graphs or sparse undirected graphs, no algorithm faster than recomputation from scratch was known. We complement our algorithm with a conditional lower bound: Under the OMv conjecture, any insertions-only algorithm that outputs the current value of $κ$ after every insertion needs $Ω(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ amortized time per edge insertion for $κ= Θ(n)$. Previous conditional lower bounds for this problem only apply to worst case running time, or algorithms that support both edge insertions and edge deletions.

papers.title: A ${}^{13}$CO Detection in a Massive Molecular Gas Flow in Abell 1795's Central Galaxy
papers.abstract: We present new ALMA ${}^{13}$CO(2-1) observations of the central galaxy in the cool-core cluster Abell 1795, targeting the origin of extended molecular filaments. The filaments extend for 5--7 kpc and are closely drawn up around large radio bubbles inflated by jets from the central active galactic nucleus (AGN). Smooth velocity gradients along their lengths are consistent with entrained flows lifted by the expanding bubbles. Here we detect the northern molecular filament in the low-opacity molecular tracer ${}^{13}$CO(2-1), which can provide a more reliable measure of the molecular gas mass and conditions than ${}^{12}$CO. The velocity structure in ${}^{13}$CO(2-1) is consistent with that of the ${}^{12}$CO(2-1) emission. Using a range of plausible excitation temperatures and covering fractions, we thereby determine a filament molecular gas mass of (0.1--2) $\times \ 10^9 \ \text{M}_\odot$, or down to an order of magnitude below previous estimates. This implies a CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $α_\text{CO} =$ 0.4--5 $\ \text{M}_\odot $ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2)^{-1}$ in the filament, or $\sim$ 0.1--1 times the standard assumption of the Milky Way value. Direct entrainment by the N radio bubble is now plausible, as it can provide sufficient mechanical energy and buoyant support for the molecular gas flow. Similarly, measured X-ray cooling rates are also now consistent with in-situ condensation of uplifted, low-entropy hot gas. Both formation mechanisms require multiple generations of bubbles at higher filament masses.

papers.title: Ranking and Unranking Permutations in Heap's Order
papers.abstract: Heap's algorithm is a permutation generation method with very low constant overhead. Its element-interchanging mechanism, however, prevents the standard factorial-base Lehmer code from being applied directly, and to our knowledge no explicit Rank/Unrank algorithm for the Heap order has been published. This paper describes the block structure of Heap's algorithm in terms of rearrangement operators: the net effect of a block-internal traversal is a tail-preserving operator and the block-boundary swap is a top-level swap operator, and together they yield a closed-form recurrence for the block transitions. On this basis a bottom-up Unrank algorithm and a top-down Rank algorithm are built from one and the same closed-form in-block mapping; both run in $O(n^3)$ time and $O(n)$ space and require no factorial-scale precomputed table. The supporting proofs use a synchronized strong induction on the dimension to establish the bijectivity of the trailing-element mapping, closed forms for the final arrangement and for the trailing sequence, the dichotomy of its cycle structure, and the reciprocity of Rank and Unrank. The Heap order is in fact the colex order of the mixed-radix code.

papers.title: On the Solution Sets of the Cone-Volume Map
papers.abstract: For a fixed set $U=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ of outer unit normals, we consider the cone-volume map which associates to a vector of support numbers $b\in\mathbb R^m_{> 0}$ the cone-volume vector $γ\in\mathbb R^m$ of the polytope \[ P(U,b)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:U^\top x\leq b\}. \] We study its fibers $S(U,γ)$ over prescribed cone-volume vectors $γ$, with particular emphasis on finiteness and non-uniqueness. We give characterizations of the irreducibility of $U$ in terms of properties of the cone-volume map and its solution sets. In particular, for irreducible $U$, we show that $S(U,γ)$ is finite for all $γ$ outside a set of measure zero in the cone-volume cone, and we give an explicit upper bound for its cardinality. In the planar case, we prove that $S(U,γ)$ has semialgebraic dimension at most one for arbitrary $U$. Moreover, for every $U\in\mathcal{U}(2,m)$ with $m\geq 4$, there exists a cone-volume vector $γ$ for which $S(U,γ)$ contains at least two distinct elements. As a consequence, there exist two distinct smooth planar convex bodies with the same cone-volume measure. Finally, for $U$ in general position, we show that the number of solutions is odd for every cone-volume vector outside the exceptional set.

papers.title: Attribution-Gated Joint Estimation of Intention and Capability for Assist-as-Needed Upper-Limb Robots
papers.abstract: Assist-as-needed (AAN) control must distinguish between changes in intended motion and changes in effective voluntary torque capability, even though both can produce similar kinematic and interaction responses. A dual-measurand multimodal MHE-MPC architecture is developed as the base framework, in which the intended trajectory and the task-dependent effective voluntary torque capability are estimated online as distinct quantities, and both estimates are used to adapt robotic assistance. Building on this architecture, the ambiguity between the two update channels is formulated as a continuous credit-assignment problem and resolved by an attribution gate. A trajectory-change indicator is obtained from persistent corrective interaction, whereas a capability-change indicator is derived from the residual between normalized muscle activation and dynamics-reconstructed voluntary torque. Nine healthy participants completed factorial target-height-load trials and a pre-post fatigue cup-transport task. Without target-height input, the gated method generated correctly ordered Low-Middle-High references under every load: target changes were preferentially assigned to trajectory adaptation, whereas added load shifted adaptation toward the capability channel. It achieved the lowest RMSE in all nine conditions (0.017 rad versus 0.041 rad for ungated dual estimation and 0.127 rad for fixed-reference error-based AAN). Post-fatigue capability estimates decreased and assistance increased at all heights, supporting functional feasibility.

papers.title: Rectangular Symmetry for Catalan Functions
papers.abstract: Katabolizable tableaux provide a combinatorial formula for the Schur coefficients of Catalan functions. We prove that a tableau involution preserves katabolizability under antidiagonal reflection of any upper root ideal. This involution complements shape and content in a fixed rectangle and preserves charge. We obtain a bijective proof of the rectangular symmetry of these coefficients.

papers.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
papers.abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

papers.title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Biological intelligence continually adapts to new information while retaining prior skills through localized plasticity. In contrast, continual learning in large language models (LLMs) remains vulnerable to catastrophic forgetting. A promising direction is to identify functionally specialized subnetworks within LLMs that enable targeted and resource-efficient adaptation. Using gradient-attribution profiling, we localize cognition-associated functional subnetworks exhibiting extremely low mutual overlap. Building on this finding, we propose Function-isolated Memory-Efficient Optimization (CiMEO), a continual learning framework that routes each training example to its corresponding functional subnetwork, restricting parameter updates and optimizer states to selected regions. Across 1.4 million sequential instructions, CiMEO achieves the highest average performance among the compared methods on five generative benchmarks spanning programming, examination-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Subspace-overlap and principal-angle analyses further indicate that localized updates help preserve pre-trained representations, highlighting functional subnetwork localization as a practical approach to efficient and stable continual learning in LLMs.

papers.title: Agent Status Protocol (ASP): A Lightweight Specification for State Reporting in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: The Agent Status Protocol (ASP) defines a lightweight way for heterogeneous AI agents to report their operational state to a status server, and for observers such as dashboards to receive that state as soon as it changes. Agents push small JSON events over HTTP POST; the server exposes the aggregated state to observers over Server-Sent Events (SSE). Because an agent that has crashed, hung or been compromised cannot be trusted to report its own failure, ASP does not rely on self-reports alone: the server infers liveness from missed heartbeats, can detect agents that are alive but no longer making progress, and accepts observations from supervisors, guardrails, operators and peers, some of which take precedence over what the agent says about itself while others are shown alongside it. ASP models state along independent dimensions (lifecycle, health, task, floor, governance), so that an agent can be, for example, online, degraded, working on a task and waiting for the floor at the same time. It reuses existing vocabularies: task states from the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, floor states from the Open Floor Protocol (OFP), and attribute conventions from the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. This paper presents version 0.1 of ASP as a proposal, not as an approved standard. It is a working draft intended to open a discussion, and the authors invite comments, alternative proposals and independent implementations from the community.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
papers.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

papers.title: Pricing the Unprovable: Ambiguity, Turnstile Runs, and the Verifiability Discount in Crypto Protocols
papers.abstract: Privacy-preserving protocols can repair a vulnerability without establishing whether it was exploited beforehand, even when no theft is reported and aggregate supply is protected. We call the potential value reduction from this gap the verifiability discount. A turnstile model shows how early withdrawal can shift a possible shortfall to remaining holders and why credible evidence can become more valuable as exposure grows. We introduce VDISC, a reproducible framework that records reported loss, exposed value, public evidence, returns, and pool flows separately. It combines Orchard's staged disclosures with reconstructed on-chain flows, earlier Zcash cases, and a 40-event security panel. Orchard follows the predicted direction: market responses were muted after repair and supply assurance, while the largest negative return and aggregate shielded-pool net outflow aligned with the acknowledgment that past abuse could not be ruled out. These patterns are directional, not causal. Across events, market-cap-normalized reported loss and unresolved exposure overlap among the 38 events with a public loss figure (Pearson 0.86, Spearman 0.56), partly because exposure is often coded from the loss itself, so returns alone cannot distinguish reported loss from unresolved history. The findings motivate three candidate design priorities: produce privacy-compatible evidence about past states, limit the state exposed by a single flaw, and disclose residual uncertainty explicitly.

papers.title: A Systematic and Validated Translation of the Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale to Chinese
papers.abstract: The Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale (PETS) allows evaluation of empathic behavior in intelligent systems, a concept increasingly applied in human-AI interaction, particularly in emotional and mental health support applications. To support intercultural research and development, PETS is already available in multiple languages, as research suggests cultural and language-based differences in the expression and perception of empathy. Given the substantial Chinese-speaking population and the growing focus on cross-cultural HCI research, we present a validated translation of PETS into Putonghua (Mandarin) with Simplified Chinese. Based on established back-translation methodologies as used in previous PETS translations, our process included multiple independent translations, expert panel reviews, and empirical testing with a total of N=400 participants from an English and a Chinese sample. Through confirmatory factor analysis and invariance testing we show that the Chinese PETS retains the original two-factor structure with high reliability, with support for configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Beyond validation, empathic system behavior was rated equivalently across languages, while non-empathic behavior drew substantially higher ratings from Chinese participants, suggesting its absence is read less consistently across cultures than its presence. This validated Chinese version enables researchers and practitioners to assess empathy perceptions among Chinese-speaking users, supporting culturally appropriate empathic technology development.

papers.title: Imaging defects in two-dimensional crystals by convergent beam electron diffraction
papers.abstract: Convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED), recently demonstrated on two-dimensional (2D) materials, offers a number of interesting applications such as imaging atomic in- and out-of plane shifts, interlayer distances, and individual adsorbates. In this study, we show how CBED allows for atomic-precision imaging of individual defects in 2D materials using one single-shot intensity measurement. In combination with structural calculations using density functional theory, we present simulated CBED patterns for various defects in graphene, each of which exhibits a unique fingerprint distribution. We also show how atomic positions, including the individual atomic defects in graphene, can be reconstructed by iterative phase retrieval from a single CBED pattern.

papers.title: Spectral Theory for Schrodinger Operators with Interface Transmission Conditions
papers.abstract: Interfaces influence transport across biological membranes, habitat boundaries, and composite media. Motivated by these applications, we study two classes of Schrodinger eigenvalue problems with transmission conditions allowing jumps in the solution or its normal derivative. We develop a weighted variational framework that accommodates asymmetric interface coupling and yields self-adjoint realizations in suitable weighted Hilbert spaces. For both problems and their adjoints, we establish discrete spectra, variational eigenvalue characterizations, and eigenfunction completeness in arbitrary spatial dimensions. We prove spectral continuity and identify limiting spectra in singular parameter regimes. We also extend Courant's nodal domain theorem to eigenfunctions that may be discontinuous across the interface. The spectral results further extend to divergence-form elliptic operators under suitable assumptions on the coefficients. These results provide a foundation for analyzing elliptic and parabolic equations with interface transmission conditions.

papers.title: On the variety of sum of powers of certain complete intersection forms
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a homogeneous polynomial (form). If the annihilator ideal $F^\perp$ is a complete intersection, then $F$ is called as a complete intersection form. For many complete intersection forms, we show that its minimal apolar ideal is a complete intersection and further we show that ${\rm VSP}(F)$ is irreducible and compute its dimension.

papers.title: Generic Mean Curvature Flow With Rough Weights
papers.abstract: We prove the generic existence of mean curvature flows in spaces with rough weights. Our weak solutions are both unit-density Brakke flows and distributional solutions. Such a generic statement is optimal in the sense that we consider weights that are too rough to have well-defined traces on every hypersurface.

papers.title: Quantitative validation of SMBI deposition profiles on EAST using experimentally constrained simulations
papers.abstract: Quantitative comparison between SMBI fueling simulations and experiments has long been hampered by the poor constraint on the effective source. Here, the particle increment per pulse is extracted experimentally and used to calibrate the simulation source. For EAST shot 71438, the density evolution from microwave reflectometry is analyzed for nine SMBI pulse groups. The SMBI-induced density increase is isolated from the background by comparing the rising and falling phases around each pulse group. Its radial profile peaks in the mid-pedestal region for every pulse group. Volume integration of this increment provides the experimental reference. The simulations use a multi-fluid model in the BOUT++ framework in which two transport operators are recast into conservative flux form, with the particle balance residual reduced to about 2% of the injected amount, and the perpendicular transport coefficients are constructed from the discrete radial flux balance, with the unphysical changes of the initial density and temperature profiles in source-free evolution reduced by an order of magnitude. For three cases sharing the same nominal molecular flux, the simulated deposition peak agrees with the experimental one in the relative pedestal coordinate. The simulated conversion of the injected particles at the end of the injection is slightly lower than the value inferred from the experiment, while the fraction retained at the end of the pulse is higher. The perturbation thus decays more slowly in the simulation, which we attribute to fast loss channels not represented in the model, such as parallel losses to the scrape-off layer. The edge electron temperature stays on the high-temperature plateau of the dissociation and ionization rate coefficients throughout the pulse, and the inward shift of the deposition with edge cooling reported earlier does not occur under the present conditions.

papers.title: Federated Art Chase: Privacy Leakage and Data Poisoning in Federated Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly used to adapt a pretrained, centrally fine-tuned model to data that remain on user devices, beyond training a model from scratch. In this report, prepared for the 4th Federated Machine Learning International Summer School, we study the privacy and integrity of this approach with a reproducible pipeline. An ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV4-Conv-Small model is fine-tuned centrally on ten Quick, Draw! classes (97.50% test accuracy) and then adapted with head-only FedAvg over ten non-IID clients, which raises client training accuracy from 90.34% to 91.49% while preserving global accuracy. We evaluate four adversarial scenarios. First, from a single one-step client update, an honest-but-curious server recovers the complete private label set, but its reconstructions follow class prototypes rather than the private drawings (mean SSIM 0.130). Second, from a one-round FedAvg aggregate, label-count recovery falls from 87.5% with one client to 75.0% with five and ten clients, below the 80.0% of an uninformed uniform guess. Third, under FedAvg, a backdoor injected by 30%, 50%, and 100% of the clients reaches an attack success rate (ASR) of 21.9%, 31.3%, and 54.7% at a cost of at most 0.8 percentage points of clean accuracy, whereas label flipping is effective only when most of the source-class data are relabeled. Fourth, FLTrust with a root set retained from centralized fine-tuning lowers the backdoor ASR to 1.8% and 4.0% at 30% and 50% malicious clients and the label-flipping ASR from 12.6% to 0.8% without measurable clean-accuracy loss, but provides no protection when every client is malicious. The report closes with a live session in which participants draw, fine-tune, and poison the model through Indigma's FedMaestro orchestrator. Code and executed notebooks, runnable on Google Colab, are at https://github.com/Indigma-Innovations/fl-summer-school.

papers.title: How do late-time photons "record" primordial curvature perturbations?
papers.abstract: Inflationary cosmology faces a fundamental gap between primordial quantum fluctuations and the classical cosmic history inferred from observations. Although the primordial quantum state is a superposition of field configurations, standard cosmology assumes one definite realization of curvature perturbations and uses classical perturbation theory to describe the resulting gravitational potentials, CMB anisotropies, and large-scale structure. Squeezing and decoherence of primordial fluctuations alone do not explain why this one-realization description is physically meaningful. We address this issue through Cosmological Classical Branches (CCBs), using the quantum-information-theoretic notion of physical records. In CCBs, distinct late-time matter components carry compatible records of the same primordial configuration. A record in one component makes that configuration readable, while a disjoint compatible record suppresses interference accessible to operations on the first. Each branch thus admits a common c-number primordial label at finite resolution, while the global quantum superposition persists. This Letter summarizes the framework developed in Ref.~\cite{Kuroda2026CCB}.

papers.title: Finite-Time Guarantees for Constrained Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: We study reinforcement learning in constrained partially observable Markov decision processes (CPOMDPs), where an agent maximizes reward subject to a cost constraint using only incomplete information about the underlying state. The lack of state observability may require optimal policies to depend on arbitrarily long observation-action histories, making planning and learning challenging. We leverage recent advances in finite-memory approximations of POMDPs and represent finite history windows as states of a constrained MDP. We then develop a primal--dual algorithm that provides the first non-asymptotic guarantees that jointly bound average reward suboptimality and constraint violation in the original CPOMDP. A key challenge is that this finite-window approximation affects both reward values and the set of feasible policies. Under a filter-stability assumption, we derive bounds relating optimality and feasibility in the finite-state model to those in the original CPOMDP, with approximation errors that decay geometrically with the window length. Experiments in partially observable gridworlds demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: When Is Muon Optimal? Radial Fragility and Minimax Geometry
papers.abstract: Muon replaces a matrix gradient by an approximate polar factor and has shown strong empirical performance in neural-network training. The Isotropic Curvature Model (ICM) provides a curvature-based explanation for this update by asking when gradient orthogonalization minimizes a one-step local-loss surrogate. We investigate the stability of this explanation when the fixed input radius of the ICM is replaced by a general radial law. We introduce the Random-Radius Isotropic Curvature Model (RR-ICM) and the Polar-Factor Admissibility Set, which encodes exact scaled-polar optimality as a geometric condition on the positive polar factor of the gradient. We derive an exact characterization of this set for arbitrary radial laws and show that all nonscalar admissible responses arise from radial atoms aligned with curvature kinks. Consequently, every atomless radial law exhibits zero-capacity rigidity: exact scaled-polar optimality is possible only when the gradient is already a scaled column isometry. To connect the curvature-based framework with the established spectral geometry of Muon, we introduce the Minimax RR-ICM by replacing directional averaging with worst-case optimization over probability laws on the sphere. We prove that every nonzero global minimizer lies on the polar ray of the gradient, while its scale is determined by a one-dimensional convex problem. The corresponding admissibility geometry is a positive-semidefinite trace slab, in sharp contrast to the spherical-zonoid geometry of the RR-ICM. Together, these results expose the radial fragility of average-curvature explanations and provide a new minimax variational characterization of Muon's polar direction.

papers.title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance for TI2I Flow Matching
papers.abstract: We study Text-and-Image-to-Image (TI2I) flow matching methods for controllable image editing. In a broader generative modeling context, Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is established as a key component responsible for high quality outputs. However, we argue that its role in TI2I modeling is poorly understood. Specifically, we make the surprising observation that the CFG mechanism is implicitly harmful for editing in the noisy phase of flow modeling, hindering instruction following and controllability. We propose a simple correction in the early flow steps, enabling a richer alignment-preservation tradeoff at no extra cost. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated on both pixel-space and latent TI2I flows.

papers.title: Estimators from Convex Geometries of the Simplex
papers.abstract: We unify several geometries of the probability simplex under one principle, their generation by a potential: convex potentials produce the Bregman divergences and dually flat structures of information geometry, and the exponentially concave potentials of Pal and Wong produce the logarithmic divergences and their projectively flat structures. Each structure carries a duality between maximum entropy and minimum divergence and, with it, a projection principle for estimation: the U-estimators of Eguchi, Komori and Ohara in the first case, the λ-deformed estimators of Wong and Zhang in the second, both governed by a Pythagorean relation and reducing to maximum likelihood in the undeformed limit. We complete the picture with estimators drawn from the third connection the divergence defines, the Levi-Civita one, by minimizing geodesic distance: existence, uniqueness and influence are then controlled by curvature and diameter rather than by flatness. Along the way the Aitchison geometry appears as the logarithmic-barrier instance of the construction at its critical weight, and the symmetrization of the Pal-Wong transport cost, a smoothing of the Hilbert projective metric, is shown to lose the dual pair and to support instead a Huber-type robust center with bounded influence in a geometry of infinite diameter.

papers.title: Minimum RISC-V: Maximum FPGA Efficiency
papers.abstract: RISC-V processors are now widely available for FPGAs, with most FPGA vendors replacing their proprietary soft-CPU architectures with this instruction-set architecture (ISA). Although contemporary FPGAs are increasingly resource- and feature-rich, a soft processor system---including memory---often occupies a disproportionately large footprint and delivers only modest performance relative to the potential of the target device. In this work we first design a lightweight but deeply pipelined RISC-V core that can run above 700 MHz in a mid-range device and that is capable of retiring one instruction per clock under ideal conditions. We then develop and demonstrate a new optimization method that compiles the final application binary and a specialized processor instance contemporaneously. The method expands each instruction into an application-specific encoding, removes unused datapath and decode logic during synthesis, and yields cores that remain assembler-compatible with the original program while no longer being binary-compatible with a general-purpose RISC-V. We implement example designs on RV32I (base integer), RV32M (integer multiply), and RV32F (single-precision floating-point) configurations. Our optimized RISC-V is as small as 170 ALMs and closes timing at 775 MHz in an Altera Agilex-5 device. Finally, we show that these processors can be packed into a deterministic area and stepped-and-repeated continuously without material impact on performance, enabling predictable multi-core density planning.

papers.title: Writability and the Pathway: A Controlled Study of Knowledge Injection into Addressed Memory
papers.abstract: Addressed conditional memory provides a local surface for post-hoc knowledge injection, but a successful write need not transfer to a new question or preserve untargeted behavior. This study combines a controlled GPT-2 comparison with production-memory experiments on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Newly initialized modules attached to frozen GPT-2 are tested in a 2 x 2 design: row-only versus row-plus-projection updates, each with or without fixed module-residual anchoring. All arms reproduce 50 trained completions in each of three sampling seeds. Natural-question target-string hits average 5.3% for both row-only arms, 28.7% for unanchored projection updates, and 22.0% with anchoring, while strict answer scores remain zero. Anchoring lowers measured drift; lexical hits do not establish entity-specific retrieval. In the archived Qwen experiments, gradient writes make the designated first answer token top-ranked for 132 independently reset targets, comprising 93 new promotions and 39 already top-ranked targets. A separate matched 24-target comparison gives 13 new promotions with Adam versus two with SPSA at equal iteration counts but unequal computational procedures. An 80-row case includes saved continuations and a replay record, while reformulations bound its scope. Six DeepSeek zero-order cases yield one new target-token promotion and one regression. These results support bounded writing feasibility and separate trained expression, question-form behavior, and preservation; first-token rankings do not establish complete-answer success or universal conditions for writable memory.

papers.title: EviGround-CT: Sentence-to-Volume Grounding for Verifying LLM-Generated Chest CT Reports
papers.abstract: Chest computed tomography (CT) reports generated by large language models (LLMs) can describe positive findings that lack localized evidence in the scan. We propose EviGround-CT to verify these findings after report generation. A deterministic extractor identifies positive finding sentences, and a 3D grounding model predicts an evidence mask for each sentence. Using the full sentence retains anatomical location, laterality, and descriptive modifiers in the grounding query. We evaluate report generation on CT-RATE, and grounding and verification on a held-out 100-case ReXGroundingCT subset. Using the available annotations, sentence-grounded verification raises evidence-supported precision (ESP) from 0.263 to 0.365 across 137 extracted in-scope positives, compared with category conditioning. The corresponding unsupported positive finding rate falls from 0.737 to 0.635. The paired case-level bootstrap ESP difference is +0.102 (95% confidence interval: [0.028, 0.181]). The predicted masks associate individual report statements with spatial evidence that can be inspected alongside the CT.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification
papers.abstract: Instead of learning a mapping from instances to outcomes in the standard way, the key idea of pairwise difference learning (PDL) is to learn a function that takes two instances as input and predicts the difference between the respective outcomes. Given a function of this kind, predictions for a query instance are derived from every training example and then averaged. We propose a version of PDL for the task of classification and propose a suitable meta-learning technique for this purpose. Moreover, we address the problem of uncertainty quantification, i.e., of representing and quantifying the uncertainty of a PDL classifier's predictions in a faithful manner. Building on recent work on the decomposition of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components, we propose different ways of extending corresponding measures to the setting of PDL, depending on how and to what extent uncertainty is represented by the underlying base learner. In large-scale empirical studies, we analyze both the predictive accuracy and the uncertainty awareness of our PDL classifier.

papers.title: When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark
papers.abstract: Muon's gains in data efficiency motivate evaluating its performance under explicit data, time, and tuning budgets. On a single A100 GPU, we compare a reference single-device Muon implementation with AdamW across 17.7M- and 33.6M-parameter causal language models and 2.70M-parameter vision transformers. A common 23-candidate development budget selects configurations evaluated with five matched seeds, full validation trajectories, optimizer-step timing, and a frozen one-shot test. Muon reduces validation-loss area under the curve by 3.25--22.44\% at equal data and lowers test loss in all 20 primary pairs. In this configuration, Muon improves time-normalized loss area} by 19.68--22.31\% on vision, while AdamW is better by 3.38--6.96\% on language. The full Muon optimizer call, including auxiliary AdamW updates, consumes 56.1--69.6\% of training time, compared with 6.1--9.1\% for the AdamW baseline. Muon also has higher expected regret under restricted access to these candidate pools. These results characterize small models with reference kernels; their wall-clock ordering does not establish a ranking for larger models or optimized implementations.

papers.title: Finite-Frequency Boson-Number Bounds Across the Quantum Rabi Transition
papers.abstract: We consider the quantum Rabi model, a fundamental model of quantum optics describing a two-level system coupled to a bosonic mode, including counter-rotating terms. In the limit of large separation between the two-level transition frequency and the bosonic mode frequency, the model exhibits a quantum phase transition at a critical coupling strength. Although the model is exactly solvable, simple analytic expressions for important physical quantities are generally unavailable. We derive rigorous upper and lower bounds for the ground-state energy and boson occupation number across the quantum phase transition at finite frequency ratios. Our results characterize the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes and establish the scaling behavior of the boson occupation near the critical point. Exact numerical diagonalization demonstrates the tightness of the derived bounds, while the resulting finite-frequency inequalities provide experimentally testable predictions for trapped-ion quantum simulators.

papers.title: Reducing the Cost of Qudit State Preparation by Learning a Sparse Structure for SNAP Gates
papers.abstract: Preparing quantum states in bosonic qudits with SNAP--Displacement sequences requires both optimizing the gate parameters and deciding which Fock levels should be controlled by each SNAP gate. A fully parameterized ansatz assigns an independent phase to every Fock level in every gate, leading to a number of phases that grows steeply. This constitutes a problem for short to medium term systems as controlling many phases requires complex control pulses which are subject to increased control errors. Previous work reduced this cost by restricting the trainable phases to predefined sparse patterns, such as a diagonal or a grid, which however may not be optimal for a specific target state. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a method that learns which phases are needed together with their values, using a differentiable mask. A sparsity penalty encourages the removal of unnecessary phases, while temperature annealing gradually turns the masks into binary decisions. We compare the proposed method with fully parameterized and predefined sparse ansatzes on Fourier and Haar-random target states. The evaluation considers both the minimum number of phases required to reach different infidelity thresholds and the overall trade-off between fidelity and phases required, measured through Pareto frontiers and hypervolume. The results show that learning the location of the phases together with their values provides competitive or improved fidelity--resource trade-offs, although the advantage depends on the target state and qudit dimension.

papers.title: Mobility energetic balance frames spatial configuration of cities
papers.abstract: Urban spatial configurations emerge as the result of interactions between citizens' activities, movements and the landscape. Topography forms part of the physical settings through which mobility occurs, influencing movement energetic requirements. Using road networks, elevation data and mobility flows inferred from geolocated records, we define a simplified comparative measure of movement energy and test how it changes when the observed urban configuration is translated, rotated or rescaled within its topographic setting while mobility demand is held fixed. Across 56 cities, observed configurations consistently show lower movement energy requirements than most of the alternative configurations examined. This recurrent pattern reveals a measurable relationship between topography and urban spatial organization and is compatible with cumulative adaptation among urban structure, mobility and terrain. These findings add an energetic dimension to our understanding of how topography relates to urban spatial organization and provide an empirical basis for considering terrain-related movement requirements when evaluating future urban growth and densification.

papers.title: Density of repelling periodic points for cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: We prove the repelling-density conjecture for cubic rational maps over $\mathbf C_p$: for every prime $p$, the classical Julia set is the closure of the classical repelling periodic points. By Bézivin's theorem, it suffices to prove that a nonempty classical Julia set contains a classical repelling periodic point. The case $p\geq5$ follows from known results for tame maps, so we treat residue characteristics two and three. We argue by contraposition, assuming that the map has no classical repelling periodic points. Maps with potential good reduction already have empty classical Julia set. Otherwise, we conjugate the map to an explicit normalized form and analyze its coefficients. In each case, we obtain coefficient restrictions and establish a uniform bound on the spherical derivatives of all iterates. This bound implies equicontinuity on the classical projective line and hence emptiness of the classical Julia set.

papers.title: Numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
papers.abstract: A confident detection of orbital eccentricity in gravitational-wave signals from black hole-neutron star systems would be a strong indicator of their dynamical formation origin. While eccentric waveform models have recently been developed, their validity for analyzing black hole--neutron star signals has yet to be tested against numerical-relativity simulations. Building upon our previous study of quasicircular black hole--neutron star mergers, we perform simulations of a subset of these systems with orbital eccentricities around five times larger than those inferred for GW200105_162426. Additionally, we perform simulations with magnetized matter to assess whether trapped $g$-mode oscillations persist in strongly magnetized disks. Regarding the emitted gravitational-wave signal, we find that the effective one-body waveform model SEOBNRv5EHM shows reasonable agreement unless tidal contributions become important, and the inspiral-only post-Newtonian models pyEFPE/pyEFPEHM show larger disagreement in the late inspiral. For the equal-mass system, which has the largest effective tidal deformability, eccentric tidal corrections have a small but noticeable impact on the phase, $\sim0.1$ rad. We find an almost negligible impact of eccentricity on the properties of the remnant black hole, and differences of up to a factor of two in the remnant disk mass. Trapped $g$ modes in the accretion disks have the same frequency regardless of the eccentricity, confirming that they depend mainly on the properties of the remnant black hole. We find that when accretion disks are strongly magnetized, they become less dense and have less pronounced structure, and that the trapped $g$ modes previously identified in the unmagnetized cases are efficiently damped.

papers.title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed as conversational agents are increasingly expected to follow procedural logic. While factual hallucination has received extensive attention, a different failure mode has been overlooked: procedural hallucination, in which an agent produces individually fluent and factually plausible utterances while deviating from the intended conversational process. We introduce DialFork, the first benchmark to measure this failure mode on raw dialogue text. DialFork is built by forking conformant dialogues at controlled turn positions and injecting one of four hallucination types, yielding 36,278 dialogues across 24 tasks in 12 domains; 30 human annotators validate the construction. We define three evaluation tasks that characterize procedural deviation at three granularities: how far a set of dialogues deviates from conformant ones (monitoring deployed agents), how far a single dialogue does (procedural retrieval), and at which turn a dialogue first goes off-track (real-time guardrails). For the first two, we propose dialog-flow-aware metrics, FlowKL and FlowScore, that compare dialogues by how they unfold rather than their content. At the dialogue level, FlowScore significantly outperforms all baselines across seven encoders, showing that semantic similarity is no substitute for procedural similarity. We release DialFork under open licenses at https://github.com/idiap/dialfork, hoping the community will measure conversational process alongside content.

papers.title: A Quantum Machine Learning Approach to Content-Based Media Recommendation
papers.abstract: We use quantum machine learning techniques to develop a content-based media recommender system and evaluate its performance on TV programmes using textual descriptions from one week of BBC iPlayer data. Grounded in the Quantum Natural Language Processing framework (QNLP), programme synopses are mapped to variational quantum circuits using their semantic structure. The parameters of these circuits are trained via a supervised pairwise similarity learning task. We benchmark the quantum recommender against a classical BiLSTM baseline trained on the same dataset and objective. While both models achieve comparable performance on the similarity learning task, the quantum model requires significantly fewer parameters (47k vs. 17.8M). When the BiLSTM is constrained to a matching parameter budget, its performance degrades substantially (by 3.63 percentage points in Mean Average Precision (MAP)), indicating that the structured quantum representation provides a highly parameter-efficient alternative in this setting. We demonstrate the feasibility of executing the trained models on quantum hardware by deploying the circuits on Quantinuum's System Model H2 (and accompanying emulator) using a SWAP-test-based protocol. The results confirm that the similarity signal is preserved under realistic, noisy conditions. Taken together, these findings highlight the potential of variational quantum circuits for recommendation tasks and represent a practical step toward their real-world deployment.

papers.title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
papers.abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier.
