We also compare these injection shares with the earlier studies that proposed an essential role for $E>B$ regions. We conclude that $E>B$ regions are neither necessary for injection nor the dominant direct contributors to pre-injection work by injection share in two-dimensional, nonradiative pair-plasma reconnection at vanishing guide field.

papers.title: Compliant GMT: Making General Motion Tracking Compliant via Residual Reference Adaptation
papers.abstract: We propose Compliant GMT (C-GMT), a modular framework for full-body compliant responses in general motion tracking. As humanoid robots move into real world deployment, they not only need to perform any motion but also respond safely and robustly to interaction forces. Existing general motion tracking policies can imitate diverse motions but are trained to be stiff, leading to unexpected and unsafe behaviors under disturbance. Prior work in compliant humanoid control trades off compliance and generality. There exist examples of full-body compliant responses, but these are heavily curated to single-reference policies. On the other hand, general motion trackers (GMT) are trained to rigidly imitate massive motion capture datasets. Our key insight is to leverage the generality of pretrained GMTs for motion tracking while introducing compliance from a residual adapter that conditions on a history of proprioception. This enables our approach, C-GMT, to achieve both general motion tracking and whole-body compliant responses. Compared to state-of-the-art general motion trackers and single-motion compliant policies, C-GMT demonstrates competitive performance in both motion tracking accuracy and compliance adherence. We further demonstrate improved safety, robustness, and error tolerance in simulation and real-world G1 experiments.

papers.title: Scene Reconstruction Using Ubiquitous Wireless Signals via Diffusion Posterior Inference Over physics-Grounded Representations
papers.abstract: Knowing the layout of the physical world matters for many applications, yet the sensors we rely on for it (e.g., cameras and LiDAR) can fail in darkness, in adverse weather, or behind walls. Wireless signals do not face these limitations: every link between a base station and a user is shaped by the buildings it passes, reflects from, or is blocked by, leaving information about the surrounding scene embedded in the wireless channel measured at the endpoints. However, mapping channel measurements to the environment is a severely ill-posed problem: a measurement records only the structures that interact with the transmitted electromagnetic waves along its propagation paths, and even these observations can often be explained by multiple plausible scenes. We therefore formulate wireless scene reconstruction as posterior inference and develop a hierarchical framework with two complementary stages to approach this problem. A wireless foundation model, pretrained to respect propagation physics, transforms each channel measurement into a representation of the scene structure that shaped the observation. A diffusion model then jointly integrates representations from multiple measurements to model and sample the posterior over building occupancy, with consensus over samples producing the final reconstruction. We demonstrate that the framework can accurately recover building footprints from wireless channel measurements alone and show that its performance depends critically on both design components: physics-grounded representations expose scene-relevant information, while joint posterior inference coherently integrates complementary observations.

papers.title: Locally indicable groups outside Brodskiĭ's quasivariety
papers.abstract: We provide a set of group properties that together obstruct membership in the quasivariety that Brodskiĭ constructed in his proof that torsion-free one-relator groups are locally indicable. There are examples of locally indicable groups with these properties, which implies that Brodskiĭ's quasivariety is strictly contained in the quasivariety of all locally indicable groups. This disproves a conjecture of Howie.

papers.title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery
papers.abstract: Genetic and drug perturbation screens are important tools for elucidating disease mechanisms and validating therapeutic targets, but experimental costs limit the number of candidates that can be tested. Existing perturbation screening methods typically update the surrogate model with feedback while keeping the acquisition function fixed, limiting their ability to adapt selection to different response landscapes. Experimental feedback reveals current hits and informs subsequent selection by updating candidate predictions, providing a training signal for learning how to select experiments. We formulate budgeted perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem and propose Temporal Difference Active Learning (TDAL), which learns an acquisition function online through temporal difference learning from a single screening trajectory, accounting for current hits and future discoveries. TDAL uses the Hellinger distance between hit probabilities for unmeasured candidates before and after an experiment to weight successor value, and reuses measured outcomes through leave-batch-out (LBO) to construct virtual transitions and alleviate training data scarcity. Across eight public screens spanning single, double, and triple perturbations under varied experimental configurations, TDAL achieves an average rank of 1.63 among eleven methods and ranks first on four tasks, demonstrating its adaptability across response landscapes.

papers.title: An undecidable problem in dynamics
papers.abstract: Given a variety $X$ with a self-map $φ$ and subvarieties $Y$ and $Z$ of $X$, we consider the set of $n$ for which $φ^n(Y)$ intersects $Z$ nontrivially. Extending a beautiful construction of Lee and Nam, we show this gives rise to an undecidable problem for a fixed ambient variety $X$ and morphism $φ$. We further use this construction to give a counterexample to a conjecture of the author, Satriano, and Sierra.

papers.title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi-turn interactions. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, they are often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other requirements. However, existing evaluation methods leave a critical gap: capability benchmarks measure what agents can accomplish, while content-safety red-teaming measures harmful generations, but neither tests whether agents comply with predefined policies during otherwise valid tool use. Such policy violations are difficult to audit because their effects may emerge only after several turns, span multiple tool calls, or surface in downstream systems. We propose PROBE (Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration), an algorithm for training LLM-based auditors that interact with deployed agents as realistic users and probe them for policy violations through multi-turn, tool-mediated dialogue. We formalize agent auditing as a two-player Markov game and propose a composite reward that balances violation discovery, behavioral plausibility, conversation progress, and policy diversity. To study training objectives and reward design, we compare GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet-based optimization in a controlled setting. Across extensive experiments, auditors trained with PROBE uncover substantially broader and higher-yield policy violations than same-architecture zero-shot adversaries, even when the auditor is significantly smaller than the target agent. Our results show that multi-turn behavioral auditing is a distinct and necessary axis of agent evaluation, complementing capability and safety benchmarks. PROBE offers a scalable path toward automated policy auditing for real-world agentic systems and suggests a co-evolutionary loop in which auditors expose failures and agents improve from auditor feedback.

papers.title: Observation of the ${Ξ_b^-\to Ξ^-μ^+μ^-}$ and study of the ${Ξ_b^-\toΞ^-ψ(2S)}$ decays
papers.abstract: The rare decay ${Ξ_b^-\toΞ^-μ^+μ^-}$ is observed for the first time using proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at centre-of-mass energies of $7$, $8$ and~$13~\text{TeV}$, corresponding to integrated luminosities of $1$, $2$ and $6~\text{fb}^{-1}$, respectively. Its branching fraction is reported in intervals of the dimuon invariant mass squared. The integrated value of ${\cal{B}}(Ξ_b^-\toΞ^-μ^+μ^-)$ is measured to be ${ (118 \pm 24 \pm 7 \pm 38 ) \times 10^{-8}}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical, the second is systematic and the third uncertainty arises from the normalisation branching fraction ${\cal{B}}(Ξ_b^-\toΞ^-J/ψ)$, whose uncertainty is dominated by SU(3)-breaking effects. In addition, the ratio of the branching fractions of the ${Ξ_b^-\toΞ^-ψ(2S)}$ and the ${Ξ_b^-\toΞ^-J/ψ}$ decays is measured to be ${ 0.491 \pm 0.041 \pm 0.019 }$.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca

papers.title: A Quad Beam Variable Height Antenna System for Reliable Underground Mine Tunnel Communications
papers.abstract: Mine accidents can damage the wired backbone supporting underground wireless networks, forcing rescue teams to deploy temporary mesh nodes to maintain communication with the surface. Although higher carrier frequencies can support bandwidth-intensive applications such as live video, multimode propagation within mine tunnels produces severe, spatially localized fading. Movable antennas can mitigate these fades by adjusting antenna position; however, moving all antennas on a multi-link relay node simultaneously may improve one link at the expense of another. This paper introduces QuadBeam, a compact mesh node antenna system comprising four independently positionable 2.4~GHz patch antennas mounted on the side faces of a central hub, together with a 900~MHz monopole for backup voice communication. A preliminary prototype incorporates one motor-driven patch mount and three manually adjustable mounts. Bench measurements show interelement coupling below $-46$~dB between patches on adjacent faces. Measurements at five carrier frequencies from 2.40~GHz to 2.48~GHz in the Edgar Experimental Mine reveal 19~dB to 26~dB received-power variations across transmitter and receiver separations of 8.3~m to 18.3~m. Adjusting the receiver height over approximately 20~cm yields received-power improvements of up to 22~dB. Repositioning neighboring patches and removing or reinstalling the monopole produce no noticeable change in the active link. These results demonstrate the potential of independently positioned antennas to alleviate spatial fading in underground mesh communications.

papers.title: Causal Integrated Gradients: Scalable Feature Attribution Along Causal Paths
papers.abstract: Existing feature attribution methods that account for feature dependencies do not scale to high dimensions. We propose causal integrated gradients (CIG) and causal expected gradients (CEG), which extend integrated gradients to incorporate prior causal structure among input features while retaining its computational efficiency and, under conditions on the causal graph, its axiomatic guarantees. In many settings, some causal structure between features is already known, for example, that a transcription factor causally regulates a target gene's expression. Yet existing gradient-based methods cannot exploit this structure, instead crediting a feature's downstream effects over its true upstream cause, such as ranking the target gene above the transcription factor that regulates it. Our key idea is to embed this causal structure by routing the integration path along the causal graph. The method thereby decomposes each feature's attribution into a direct effect and effects mediated through its causal descendants. We evaluate CIG in three settings of increasing realism. First, on a synthetic benchmark with a known causal model, CIG's attributions best match the ground-truth causal effect from Pearl's do-calculus, matching the accuracy of causal Shapley values at a fraction of the computational cost. Second, on simulated single-cell gene expression data with a known gene regulatory network (Dyngen), CIG most accurately recovers the transcription factors driving the simulation. Third, on real interferon-$β$ stimulation data, where only an approximate causal graph is available, CIG better prioritizes the transcription factors driving the measured response than DeepSHAP and integrated gradients. Together, these results show that incorporating causal structure into gradient-based attributions recovers upstream drivers that existing methods miss, without sacrificing scalability.

papers.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
papers.abstract: Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it. We propose to personalize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization. We adapt three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non-personalized model. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model's behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features.

papers.title: The gravitational constant and the cosmic microwave background
papers.abstract: The CMB constrains the gravitational constant $G$ at recombination to a few percent of its laboratory value, but the effect of $G$ on recombination itself is usually absorbed into a global fit rather than made explicit. We return to the semi-analytic description of the acoustic spectrum to ask how the acoustic scale $\ell_A$, the equality scale $\ell_{\rm eq}$ and the damping scale $\ell_{\rm damp}$ respond to a variation of $G$ during recombination, and where $G$ enters the residual ionization of the dark ages. We use a modified version of CLASS in which $G$ is varied through $λ_G \equiv \sqrt{G/G_{\rm N}}$, scanning $λ_G \in [0.25,2]$ at fixed physical densities and CMB temperature, with helium recomputed for each model. Analytic rate arguments are confronted with the numerical ionization histories, the visibility function, the Hu & White damping integral and the TT spectra. While $\ell_{\rm eq}$ and $\ell_A$ are nearly independent of $G$, non-equilibrium recombination gives $\ell_{\rm damp} \propto λ_G^{-0.304}$. The dependence exists only above a critical value of $G$, set by fundamental and cosmological parameters, a factor of 49 below $G_{\rm N}$. The dark-ages optical depth varies by only 16% for $G$ multiplied by 64, a negligible channel. Because $G$ enters only through the expansion rate, the imprint comes entirely from out-of-equilibrium recombination, and the competition between the atomic rates and the expansion is governed by one dimensionless combination, $α_G \equiv G m_e μ/\hbar c$, with $μ$ the mean mass of matter per photon. Each scale is the distance to last scattering divided by a length imprinted before it, so a late-time change of gravity rescales all three alike. The ratio $\ell_{\rm damp}/\ell_A$ therefore isolates $G$ at recombination and, up to lensing and screening, compares it directly with the laboratory value.

papers.title: Rovibrational cross sections for the CO$_2$ $00^00$, $01^10$, $02^20$ and Fermi resonance states $10^00(1)$ and $10^00(2)$ in collisions with He atoms
papers.abstract: We present quantum scattering calculations of CO$_2$-He state-to-state integral cross sections for 25 transition sets, covering pure rotational transitions within and rovibrational transitions between: the ground state $00^00$, the bend fundamental $01^10$, the bending overtone $02^20$, and the Fermi doublet states $10^00(1)$ and $10^00(2)$. Exact coupled-channel (CC) and coupled-states approximation (CSA) calculations are performed using a new five-dimensional potential energy surface. The calculations cover collision energies from 20 to 5220 cm$^{-1}$, sufficient to obtain converged rate coefficients over 100-800 K, and include initial rotational states for each transition up to at least $j=35$. We present an energy-grid algorithm for rovibrational quantum scattering calculations that minimizes the number of separate calculations required. The resulting cross sections exhibit a dominant $Δj=0$ propensity and parity-dependent patterns. For the benchmark $00^00,j' \leftarrow 01^10,j$ transition, thermally averaged rate coefficients reproduce available experimental data. A comparison between the CC and CSA cross sections shows that, for vibrational quenching transitions, the CSA cross sections increasingly deviate from the CC results with increasing initial rotational state $j$. Calculated integral cross sections cover collision energies and rotational states needed to derive rate coefficients for non local thermal equilibrium radiative transfer modeling of mid-infrared CO$_2$ spectra. The computationally simpler CO$_2$-He system allows the methodology and approximations to be tested at high collision energies and rotational states, helping assess their suitability for the more complex and astrochemically important CO$_2$-H$_2$ system.
authors: Floris F. S. van der Tak

papers.title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: Key-value (KV) cache management has become a critical bottleneck for scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to long-context scenarios due to linear memory growth. While recent eviction methods have moved beyond simple attention-score heuristics to incorporate value representations, they typically face a fundamental trade-off: the underlying optimization for minimizing output perturbation is an NP-hard combinatorial problem, leading to mathematically suboptimal heuristics or implementations that are difficult to kernelize. In this work, we propose DropKV, a simple principled eviction framework based on Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation. By decoupling the joint eviction decision into independent per-token scoring, DropKV circumvents combinatorial intractability and admits a provable constant-factor approximation guarantee under a cone condition that we empirically verify on three long-context LLMs. To ensure practical viability, we provide a high-performance implementation using fused Triton kernels that avoid materializing the full attention matrix, delivering a 19.8x scoring-kernel speedup that translates to up to a 9.9% matched-batch end-to-end prefill speedup. Extensive evaluations on the RULER and LongBench benchmarks demonstrate that DropKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines at equivalent cache budgets, achieving the lowest inference latency among eviction methods while also remaining faster than the dynamic cache baseline.

papers.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Interactive agents repeatedly choose among a finite set of actions, labels, or ordinal outcomes. Generating a free-form response for each choice adds latency and complicates the interface between a model and its environment. We present Intern-Decision, a family of 0.8B, 2B, and 4B multimodal decision models that return structured choices and candidate probabilities from text and optional images. Our autoregressive masked language modeling objective places one decision placeholder per field in a complete assistant JSON skeleton. Ground-truth symbols appear only in supervision, while all fields are evaluated in a single causal forward pass using the backbone's native language-model head. The 4B model achieves a 90.02% unweighted average accuracy across seven evaluation suites, compared with 88.74% for Jev v1.13.0. For a fixed 289-token request with three fields on one RTX 4090, mean latency is 44.16 ms for the 4B model and approximately 33--34 ms for the smaller models. On a separate 96-case known-distribution pilot, temperature scaling reduces expected multiclass Brier from 0.628 to 0.550 and expected calibration error from 0.213 to 0.089. A confidence-based handoff study on 111 public Jevbench-Hard items improves accuracy from 82/111 (73.87%) to 97/111 (87.39%) by routing 42 items to Atria-Dawn-Preview. We also describe qualitative game, visual interface, and browser demonstrations. These results support compact decision models as a practical component of larger agent systems.

papers.title: Unimodular Zeros of Selmer's Harmonic Trinomials
papers.abstract: Let $n>k$ be positive integers and let $\varepsilon,δ\in\{-1,1\}$. In this note, we classify the unimodular zeros of the harmonic trinomial $H_{\varepsilon,δ}:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{C}$ given by \[ H_{\varepsilon,δ}(z)=z^n+\varepsilon\overline z^{\,k}+δ, \] where $\overline{z}$ is the complex conjugate of $z\in \mathbb{C}$. Let $g:=\gcd(n,k)$ be the greatest common divisor of $n$ and $k$, and set $n_0:=n/g$ and $k_0:=k/g$. For each choice of $\varepsilon,δ\in \{-1,1\}$, we give a necessary and sufficient congruence involving $n_0$ and $k_0$ to guarantee that $H_{\varepsilon,δ}$ has unimodular zeros. More precisely, if the corresponding congruence holds, then $H_{\varepsilon,δ}$ has exactly $2g$ unimodular zeros, which are given explicitly; otherwise, it has no unimodular zeros. The proof uses a reduction to a trinomial equation and elementary divisibility arguments.

papers.title: Aspects of Anomalies: Fermion Family Constraints, Gravitational Form Factors and Scattering Amplitudes
papers.abstract: Quantum anomalies play two complementary roles in quantum field theory: as consistency conditions that constrain the field content of a theory, and as dynamical effects encoded in the analytic structure of correlation functions. This thesis explores both. In the first part, we study the 331 model, in which gauge anomalies cancel across families rather than within each one. Combined with QCD asymptotic freedom, this fixes the number of fermion generations to three. We analyze the model's symmetry breaking, scalar and flavor sectors, and its TeV-scale Landau pole. We then study the collider phenomenology of its exotic quarks, showing that the pair production of heavy quarks decaying into doubly-charged vector bileptons gives a clean same-sign dimuon plus b-jets signature, observable at a 100 TeV collider but not at the LHC. Finally, we introduce the left-right symmetric 33311 extension, which preserves the family-number constraint and avoids proton decay. In the second part, we use conformal field theory in momentum space to study the chiral, gravitational and conformal anomalies. We construct a complete off-shell parametrization of the non-Abelian TJJ correlator in perturbative QCD, identifying the dilaton-like anomaly pole. For the AVV, ATT and TJJ vertices, we prove mass-independent anomaly sum rules for the spectral density, showing that the anomaly pole is not an asymptotic particle state. We apply the TJJ insertion to the pion gravitational form factors at large momentum transfer with Sudakov resummation: the anomaly feeds mainly into the D-term and the trace form factor, improving agreement with lattice QCD. Lastly, sewing two anomaly vertices through graviton exchange, we show that the trace anomaly activates a gauge-invariant scalar gravitational channel, giving a double-copy-like structure in photon and graviton scattering.

papers.title: Asteroidal Triples and Friends in (Likely Necessary) Matrix Multiplication Time
papers.abstract: In a seminal paper, Kratsch and Spinrad [SODA 2003 and SIAM Journal on Computing 2006] studied several important problems in structural graph theory that anticipated two trends in fine-grained complexity, both from the upper- and lower-bound side: * From the upper-bound side, for each of these problems the authors give an intermediate running time strictly between $n^ω$ and $n^3$, where $ω<2.371177$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. When optimized, this running time can be made $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{(3+ω)/2})$. By now, many more problems can be solved in this running time: directed unweighted or node-weighted APSP, a variety of matrix products such as max-min and dominance, RNA Folding and many more. For some of these, the community has also developed tools suggesting that this intermediate running time is necessary. * From the lower-bound side, the authors give lower bounds of $n^{ω-o(1)}$, conditioned on three natural hardness hypotheses on the complexity of quantified variants of triangle detection that account for different types of hardness of such problems. Despite this, it has remained open for over 20 years which of these two pieces of evidence reflects the truth for the problems that Kratsch and Spinrad study: whether the intermediate running time is indeed necessary and stronger lower bounds hold, or whether the hardness evidence of Kratsch and Spinrad is essentially tight. In this paper, we resolve this question and show that the latter is the case: all problems admit an $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^ω)$ time algorithm. As an additional contribution, we make partial algorithmic progress on further problems in structural graph theory of intermediate complexity, improving over previous work [Chiu and Lu, STACS 2022 and Information and Computation 2024][Spinrad, Discrete Applied Math 2004].

papers.title: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
papers.abstract: It is common wisdom that a better understanding of how to quantify electron correlation should lead to more efficient treatments of the correlation problem. Here, we not only substantiate this view but turn it into a concrete, systematic framework for ground states. Since prominent correlation measures such as the nonfreeness depend only on the one-particle reduced density matrix, modeling the correlation energy as a function of such a measure naturally places the framework within reduced density matrix functional theory, while keeping the cost at mean-field level. Strikingly, the variable conjugate to the measure emerges as a ``correlation temperature'', thereby connecting correlation measures, functional theory, and effective temperatures. The framework rationalizes methods such as i-DMFT, and we illustrate its key concepts analytically for the Hubbard dimer and numerically for small molecular systems. This brings a fundamental question within reach: how much of the correlation problem can be solved at mean-field cost?

papers.title: Unavoidable flats in GF(q)-representable matroids
papers.abstract: We show that, for any finite field $\mathbb{F}$ and positive integer $k$, a simple $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid $M$ with sufficiently high rank contains a rank-$k$ flat which is either independent in $M$, or is a projective or affine geometry over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}$. This generalizes a result for matroids representable over prime fields due to the first two authors. As a corollary, we obtain a Ramsey theorem for matroids representable over a finite field $\mathbb{F}$. For an integer $k$, in any $2$-colouring of the points of an $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid of sufficiently high rank, there is a monochromatic rank-$k$ flat.

papers.title: Commuting Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to a characterization of commuting Toeplitz operators due to Bauer, Choe, and Koo [JFA, 268 (2015), 3017--3060]. We prove a corrected characterization for Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols of exponential type on the Fock space in one complex variable.

papers.title: CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet real-world applications often require them to continually acquire new capabilities from sequential tasks, i.e., Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT). In typical MLLMs, a projector is employed to align visual representations with the language model. However, existing methods primarily protect the language model from forgetting while continuously updating the projector across tasks. Such asymmetric adaptation can cause substantial representation drift in the projector, increasing the mismatch between the projector and language model and consequently exacerbating catastrophic forgetting. To address this issue, we propose Compatible Routing (CART), which explicitly coordinates the adaptation of the projector and language model. Specifically, CART maintains task-specific experts for both modules and combines them through weighted mixtures. CART jointly infers their weights by considering both expert relevance and cross-module compatibility, thereby promoting coordinated adaptation between the two modules. To further control model growth, we introduce relevance-guided expert consolidation, which merges experts exhibiting similar relevance profiles across samples within each module. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CART achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers.title: Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Discussions
papers.abstract: LLM systems increasingly rely on groups of agents that discuss, critique, and check one another, assuming that peers will catch individual errors. We test this assumption against a minimal adversary. In a ten-agent factual discussion, one or three adversarial agents repeatedly assert a plausible false answer. After each round we probe each benign agent's private answer through a separate call whose response is hidden from its peers, and we separately label its public stance toward the claim. Across six models and three factual-QA datasets, groups remain stable without an attacker: only 0.6% of benign agents finish with the false answer. A single adversarial agent increases this rate to 44.8% and three to 60.5%. Studies of conformity typically report public agreement without private change; we find the reverse. With three adversarial agents present, benign agents hold the false answer in 51.6% of exposed turns but publicly endorse it in only 19.7%. Much of the influence therefore remains invisible in the discussion, and the false answers persist when agents are asked for their own views. Agents that retain the true answer often fail to defend it; once adopted, the false answer spreads among benign agents, and baseline knowledge does not predict robustness.

papers.title: Are You Sure Your LLM Is Sure? Repairing and Auditing Confidence
papers.abstract: Confidence scores determine whether an LLM answer is accepted, reviewed, or regenerated, yet scalar recalibration can only correct errors visible through the score itself. We introduce RADAR (Repair, Adopt, and Diagnose After Recalibration), a reliability framework that separates confidence repair from deciding whether to deploy the repair and auditing the errors that remain. Under squared loss, we decompose prediction risk into outcome noise, information hidden by the score, and mapping error; restricting repair to order-preserving maps additionally introduces a pooling gap. For repair, we propose Probe-Anchored Isotonic Calibration (PAIC), which learns a monotone map from correctness-probe predictions on unlabeled target prompts. PAIC's excess risk depends on the probe's score-conditional bias and fitting error rather than its overall accuracy. For adoption, we derive a paired procedure with finite-sample control of false improvements. For auditing, we develop a prompt-clustered kernel test that detects feature-aligned residual errors while accounting for dependent answers from the same prompt. Across multiple LLM checkpoints, benchmarks, and distribution shifts, richer predictors can improve confidence estimation, but projecting their information back to a scalar score can lose these gains, and lower prediction risk need not yield better review decisions. Across 47,400 replayed raw-score allocations, paired betting adopts candidates with lower held-out test risk in 42.95% of allocations, versus 15.09% for one-sided empirical Bernstein. RADAR thus provides a principled workflow to repair what a scalar score can express, adopt a repair only when supported by evidence, and diagnose systematic errors that recalibration leaves behind. Code and data will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: A rigid commensurate host and a defect that switches: vacancies in the frustrated alternating spin-(1, 1/2) Heisenberg chain
papers.abstract: The alternating spin-$(1,\tfrac12)$ Heisenberg chain with a frustrating next-nearest-neighbor coupling $J_2$ loses its Lieb--Mattis moment through a discontinuous transition to a singlet whose nature was left open. Using an SU(2)-symmetric density-matrix renormalization group, in which the total spin is a quantum-number label, we identify that phase and follow a single vacancy through it. The total spin collapses directly from $S=L/4$ to $S=0$, with no partially polarized window. The singlet phase is critical: its singlet--triplet gap closes as $1/L$, its entanglement entropy grows logarithmically with a central charge $c\simeq1.8$, and its modulation wavevector, extrapolated from $L=80$ to $200$, is commensurate at $3π/4$ and independent of $J_2$ to $5\times10^{-5}$. Removing the central $S=1$ site switches the ground state of the doped chain from a triplet to a singlet at $J_2^{\ast}=0.3068(3)$, where the host shows no feature; the triplet is not bound to the vacancy but spread over one of the two segments it leaves. The transmission of correlations through the vacancy saturates at a finite value below $J_2^{\ast}$, $T(\infty)=0.102(15)$ and $0.036(9)$ at $J_2=0.28$ and $0.30$, and the cut-chain law $T\propto L^{-1}$ is excluded on both sides. We also show that the longitudinal correlator is not an observable in a triplet sector.

papers.title: Global transfer systems and endopurity of subgroups
papers.abstract: Global transfer systems are combinatorial objects that parametrize intermediate levels of structures and properties in globally equivariant homotopy theory. In this paper we study the lattice of global transfer systems, expanding beyond the case of abelian groups which was computed by the second author. The main result is a proof that the irreducible elements of the lattice of global transfer systems are strictly controlled by subgroups of groups which we refer to as endopure. From the irreducible elements one can recover the whole lattice, and studying these endopure subgroups leads us to a wide range of new phenomena and computations.

papers.title: Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Given an edge-colored graph, the wild number measures how close the graph is to having a spanning tree in every color. We investigate this parameter for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, with particular emphasis on minimum proper colorings and equitable $2$-colorings. For complete graphs, we determine the full range of wild numbers attainable by equitable $2$-colorings and show that, although every value in this range occurs, the expected wild number of a uniformly random equitable $2$-coloring tends to $0$ as the order of the graph grows. For minimum proper colorings of $K_n$, we establish a general lower bound, determine the exact wild number for $3 \le n \le 12$, and conjecture that the lower bound is sharp for all $n$. We also develop structural conditions on ideal wild sets and use them to obtain upper bounds and analyze the performance of a natural greedy algorithm. For complete bipartite graphs, we prove a sharp upper bound for equitable $2$-colorings and determine the wild number exactly for minimum proper colorings. Finally, we apply these results to Cartesian products of complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, obtaining lower bounds for the wild number under minimum proper and product colorings.

papers.title: FALCON: FPGA-Accelerated Latency-Certifiable Occupancy Networks for Camera-Based Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: A perception system that must brake for a pedestrian does not need a low average latency. It must deliver an answer before the deadline on every frame, the worst case included. Commodity edge accelerators optimize the mean through dynamic scheduling, OS jitter, thermal throttling, and contention, so their per-frame latency can be measured but not bounded. We build FALCON, a camera-based 3D occupancy front-end on the AMD Kria KR260, an embedded FPGA drawing 4.3 W idle and up to 6.6 W under inference, and make the latency guarantee layered and explicit: programmable-logic (PL) compute is cycle-bounded analytically; inference is a measured envelope over 100k-frame traces; and a watchdog enforces output delivery, publishing the previous output flagged stale when a frame is late. The deadline runs use a fixed-work proxy of six ResNet-50 DPU inferences per frame, not the full occupancy network: across three 100k-frame enforced runs, all 300k proxy frames delivered an output within the 100 ms deadline plus at most 10.2 ms, the worst of the three runs. The full six-camera FlashOcc pipeline composes to about 1.3 s per frame on the board and is not yet a 10 Hz system. The two operations the DPU cannot run, a view-transform gather and a bilinear resize, become fixed-trip-count PL IPs numerically matched to their software references. On the full Occ3D-nuScenes validation set the board reaches mIoU 29.88, 92.8% of an FP32 baseline the DPU cannot run. On a ResNet-50 probe over 100k frames the KR260 tail stays within 1.5 times its median (2.0 times for the six-inference proxy), where Jetson Orin reaches 4.4 times and the worst datacenter GPU run (NVIDIA L4) 23.6 times. The deployment recipe, HLS sources, and raw timing traces are released.

papers.title: Extending the Oracle Approximating Shrinkage to General Distributions
papers.abstract: The Oracle Approximating Shrinkage (OAS) estimator provides a closed-form, data-driven shrinkage intensity for regularizing sample covariance matrices toward a scaled identity target, but its derivation assumes Gaussian data. In practice, financial returns, neural signals, and many other high-dimensional datasets exhibit heavy tails and non-zero kurtosis, violating this assumption. We extend OAS to any distribution with finite fourth moments by incorporating a correction term $α$ built from the fourth-order joint cumulants of the data. The correction vanishes under Gaussianity, recovering the OAS formula as a special case; it admits a consistent $O(np)$ sample estimator and satisfies $ρ\in [0, 1]$ exactly for both the population cumulant and its sample analogue. Simulations and an equity-returns study confirm that the correction closes the gap between OAS and the Ledoit-Wolf estimator under non-Gaussian data, with OAS-Extended performing comparably across all tested settings. The contribution is a principled correction for OAS practitioners facing heavy-tailed data; structurally, it is distinct from prior work extending Ledoit-Wolf to elliptical distributions, which optimizes against a fixed oracle target and yields a different closed-form formula.

papers.title: Gyrators for superconducting circuit design
papers.abstract: Assuming only the solubility of Kirchhoff's laws, the conservation of energy, and the form of the constitutive relations, we present a flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism that always admits a symplectic reduction for nonsingular, well-posed circuits involving gyrators, inductors, and capacitors (LCG circuits) with arbitrary non-linearity. The formalism introduces a notion of circuit duality on non-linear non-reciprocal circuits and a family of point transformations that inserts, removes, and moves reciprocal elements across gyrators while preserving the Hamiltonian spectrum. With these transformations, we extend Tellegen's classic result that gyrators make reciprocal elements behave as their dual to non-linear reciprocal elements such as the Josephson junction and quantum phase slip. Furthermore, we present conditions under which non-reciprocal circuits can be transformed to dynamically equivalent reciprocal circuits.

papers.title: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts action-prediction latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.

papers.title: Comment on "Beam blow up due to beamstrahlung in circular e+e- colliders"
papers.abstract: The authors of the original article, Valdivia Garcia and Zimmermann (2021), state that they "derive analytical formulae for the equilibrium beam parameters, considering the varying electromagnetic field during the collision". However, to calculate the bending radius in the field of the counter-propagating bunch, they employed an approximation that is completely unjustified. Consequently, a significant portion of the formulae derived in the article bears a very tenuous relationship to reality. For practical purposes, we propose a different solution -- one that is far simpler and more accurate.

papers.title: Simulated Solvation Dynamics of a Photoexcited Organic Molecule and the Associated Time-Resolved X-ray Scattering Signal
papers.abstract: Solvation shell reorganization is a key component of the dynamics after photoexcitation of a solvated molecule, especially for charge-transfer excitation in polar solvents. These structural dynamics can be directly observed with time-resolved X-ray solution scattering (TR-XSS) experiments. However, disentangling the scattering signal of solvation-shell reorganization can be challenging, especially for systems containing only light atoms. Here, nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of a hemithioindigo chromophore in acetonitrile are used to investigate the solvation dynamics upon photoinduced charge transfer as well as vibrational excitation and cooling, and to characterize the corresponding time-resolved X-ray scattering signals. It is found that charge transfer induces rapid reorientation of the first solvation shell (0.15-0.2 ps) followed by slower reorientational and solvent redistribution within and between shells (1-2 ps). An analysis of the volume around the solute excluded to the solvent reveals an initial contraction of the solvation shell, followed by transient rebound within the first 0.4 ps, and then slower contraction. Instantaneous vibrational excitation expands the excluded volume, reaching a maximum near 0.4 ps, followed by contraction during cooling with biexponential relaxation. Low-q features in both the calculated solute-solvent and solvent-solvent scattering signals reflect rearrangements within the first solvation shell and redistribution across shells, while higher-q solute-solvent features more closely follow local first-shell restructuring. These results show that TR-XSS can provide information on both local solvent rearrangements and redistribution across solvation shells and demonstrate that interpreting the scattering signals requires accounting for changes in solvent packing induced by vibrational heating and cooling of the solute.

papers.title: MAppPrint: Robust and Real-time Mobile App Fingerprinting via Traffic Behavior Correlation Graphs
papers.abstract: Mobile apps have become ubiquitous in daily life. Despite communication encryption, app fingerprinting (AF) attacks can still enable adversaries to infer the apps in use by analyzing patterns of encrypted network traffic. However, existing AF attacks suffer from three critical limitations that hinder their practical effectiveness: (i) the inability to capture app-specific traffic dependencies, rendering traffic fingerprints fragile under dynamic networking conditions; (ii) the neglect of latency and throughput considerations, resulting in inefficient real-time user tracking; and (iii) the incapacity to handle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency. In this paper, we propose MAppPrint, a robust and real-time app fingerprinting framework. MAppPrint introduces a behavior-level traffic fingerprint, i.e., Traffic Behavior Correlation Graph (TBCG), which models app traffic by capturing unit traffic behaviors and their correlations, thereby providing reliable app fingerprints. To enable real-time fingerprinting, MAppPrint incorporates a fingerprint compression algorithm that transforms each TBCG into a compact graph by selectively aggregating redundant information. Furthermore, MAppPrint employs an unsupervised decomposition strategy to disentangle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency, enabling unified identification of both single-app and multi-app traffic. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that MAppPrint achieves 4.9~13.9% improvement in AF precision and 3~6 times improvement in timeliness over state-of-the-art methods. Meanwhile, MAppPrint is robust in dynamic networking conditions, while achieving a throughput of 10.5 GB/s and a prediction latency of 0.68 seconds.

papers.title: Smoothed analysis of policy iteration and value iteration for deterministic discounted and mean-payoff games played on any graph
papers.abstract: Our understanding of turn-based stochastic games is reminiscent of our understanding of linear programming in the 1970s. Instead of the simplex method, we have two families of algorithms - policy iteration and value iteration - which work well in practice but are known to run in exponential time on some input instances, and we still lack an algorithm that runs in polynomial time on all instances. A recent result by Loff and Skomra showed that, for deterministic discounted and mean-payoff games played on an ergodic graph, a variant of policy iteration runs in smoothed polynomial time. This offered an explanation of why policy iteration performs well in practice, analogous to Spielman and Teng's explanation for the simplex method. In this paper, we drop the ergodicity assumption: we show that their policy iteration algorithms run in smoothed polynomial time for any game graph. We do this by defining a condition number that naturally generalizes theirs, showing that sufficiently-perturbed games are well-conditioned with high probability, and showing that their algorithms are efficient on well-conditioned instances. Although the outline is similar, our proof requires a substantially new approach, based on log-Lipschitz distributions which recently appeared in work on the smoothed analysis of the simplex method. For our second contribution, we propose three new value iteration algorithms for solving deterministic mean-payoff games (also on any graph). All three are based on iterative methods for finding fixed points of non-expansive operators, which we show can be applied to the Shapley operator. The first two are simple applications of Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration and Halpern iteration. The third is quadratically faster but more complicated: it runs Zwick-Paterson and Halpern iterations in parallel. We prove that all three algorithms are correct and run in smoothed polynomial time.

papers.title: RAG-RST: Retrieved Exemplars as In-Context Discourse Schema for RST Parsing
papers.abstract: In Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST), each edge of a discourse tree carries a nuclearity label, marking which span holds the central content, and a relation drawn from a closed inventory of functional categories. Neither label is a surface property: the same two clauses can be Elaboration or Background depending on rhetorical intent, and the boundary between them is fixed by annotation convention rather than by lexical cues. Predicting these labels therefore requires a formal discourse schema, and exposure to discourse-rich pretraining text does not supply it: given only a target EDU pair, a strong LLM recovers nuclearity at 0.794 F1 and relation at 0.738 F1. We propose RAG-RST, a retrieval-augmented framework that supplies this schema as in-context demonstration rather than through parameter updates, raising nuclearity to 0.846 F1 and relation to 0.788 F1 with no training. Two configurations are compared: a precomputed strategy that labels all EDU pairs before parsing, and a dynamic strategy that retrieves at each reduce step, so that the exemplars reaching the generator depend on the reductions the parser has already committed to. Both outperform existing RST parsers across span, nuclearity, relation, and full tree metrics, with the dynamic variant consistently strongest. Two properties of the retrieved schema emerge: its utility is bounded in number, saturating and then declining beyond fifty exemplars, and it depends on structural position. Both indicate that a formal linguistic schema can be supplied to a foundation model as a demonstration rather than trained into its parameters.

papers.title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process
papers.abstract: We characterize the cases in which the minimal eigenvalues of interchange-process Laplacians on two Specht modules can be compared up to a positive multiplicative constant, independent of the edge rates. In the comparable cases, we establish an inverse-polynomial lower bound for this constant. We conjecture that the constant can always be taken to be 2/3. We apply these ideas to the mixing times of the interchange and exclusion processes. Using the comparison method of Hermon, Kozma and Salez, we prove that our conjecture implies a conjecture of Oliveira on the mixing time of the interchange process. We also obtain unconditional mixing-time bounds for both processes.

papers.title: Specification Gaming and a Constrained Reinforcement Learning Mitigation in a Cleaning Gridworld
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning agents optimize exactly the reward signal they are given, which can diverge sharply from an intended true objective when that signal is only a proxy for it; this failure mode is known as specification gaming. Existing evidence for this failure mode is largely observational, with comparatively few demonstrations pairing a controlled, deliberately constructed proxy/true gap with a mitigation that carries a verifiable guarantee rather than only an empirical improvement. We construct a minimal gridworld in which a cleaning-robot agent can either genuinely remove dirt or conceal it from a cheap sensor, and show that a standard deep Q-network trained only on the sensor's proxy reward converges to a policy that games it completely, reaching near-maximal proxy reward while never achieving the true objective. We then introduce a constrained reinforcement learning fix, penalizing the specific behaviors through which the agent exploits the gap, and show that it eliminates the gaming behavior from the final policy while substantially recovering true-objective performance. We further derive and empirically verify an exact accounting identity relating the proxy reward, true reward, and our cost signal for this environment, showing that the cost signal measures the proxy/true gap exactly rather than merely tracking it, and yields a deterministic guarantee under a hard-constrained variant of the method.

papers.title: Event-Triggered Funnel Control for Output Reference Tracking of Unknown Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: We propose an event-triggered zero-order hold implementation of the funnel controller for output reference tracking of unknown nonlinear systems. The control input is updated only when the deviation between the current and the last transmitted input exceeds a prescribed threshold, reducing the number of input updates while maintaining closed-loop performance guarantees by incorporating an auxiliary integral state to compensate for the error introduced by the zero-order-hold input. We establish a uniform lower bound on the inter-event intervals excluding Zeno behavior, and derive a growth condition on the nonlinear dynamics that ensures global existence of the solution for arbitrary, predefined sampling schedules. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical simulations.

papers.title: Integrative Thinking in Computational Physics Design Essays
papers.abstract: This study investigates integrative thinking in undergraduate computational physics design essays (CPDEs) within an engineering design-based introductory physics laboratory. Integrative thinking refers to the interaction of science, mathematics, computation, design, and metacognitive reflection during problem solving. Using the Ways of Thinking for Engineering Design-based Physics (WoT4EDP) framework, we examine how levels of integrative thinking can be characterized and manifested across teams with different levels of academic performance. We analyzed CPDEs from 14 student teams in a first-semester calculus-based physics course. Teams were grouped into high-, middle-, and low-performing categories based on members' final examination performance, enabling comparison of integrative thinking across academic performance levels. CPDEs were analyzed using thick description and an analytic rubric characterizing three levels of integrative thinking: superficial, intermediate, and substantial. Findings illustrate variation in how students coordinate multiple ways of thinking within engineering design-based physics tasks and provide a structured lens for examining integrative thinking across levels of academic performance.

papers.title: Realtime-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real-time Interactive Problems?
papers.abstract: Real-time interaction requires agents to perceive evolving environments and act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of real-time streaming models focus on conversational quality and streaming perception, leaving effective action under strict temporal constraints untested. We introduce Realtime-Bench, a suite of carefully curated dynamic tasks where delayed actions directly affect success. Under Wall Clock, where environments advance according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%, demonstrating that real-time interaction remains challenging. To separate serving latency from models' real-time streaming capability, we compare Wall Clock with Paused Clock, which removes inference delays as an idealized reference, and introduce Token Clock, which advances simulated time according to generated token counts, testing temporal awareness independently of physical serving speed. We find that temporal costs limit success in evolving environments and that higher reasoning effort has mixed effects under time pressure, reflecting a trade-off between decision quality and timely execution. Based on these results, we discuss future directions for improving real-time multimodal models, including adaptive reasoning with temporal awareness and continuous perception and action.

papers.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite group, we obtain new double affine versions of the quantum wreath Hecke algebras, and in particular of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the centre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.

papers.title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) reduce or eliminate the need for large labelled datasets by enforcing governing equations during training. Physics-informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) extend this approach to learning solution operators, enabling rapid prediction across families of problems. Despite these advantages, we show that their application to higher-dimensional problems remains limited by the computational cost of training. To address this issue, we propose a modified PI-DeepONet architecture that reduces this cost by removing redundancy in how the Branch network processes input functions across collocation points. The proposed formulation is mathematically equivalent to the original architecture but reduces input tensor sizes and the number of Branch network evaluations. We analyse the computational complexity of both architectures and derive theoretical scaling laws for training time with respect to the number of collocation points and input functions. The proposed architecture is evaluated on 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection problems. In all cases, it achieves comparable predictive accuracy to the original PI-DeepONet while consistently reducing training time. In 2D experiments, a maximum speed-up of $3.75\times$ is observed, with empirical training-time scaling agreeing with the predicted linear dependence on collocation points and input functions. Furthermore, training a 3D model on an NVIDIA A100 GPU is only feasible using the proposed architecture, as the original formulation exceeds memory limits. These results demonstrate that careful consideration of how PI-DeepONets are implemented can yield substantial gains, enhancing the practical performance of PI-DeepONets and enabling their application to otherwise intractable physics-informed learning problems.

papers.title: PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have substantially improved Text-to-SQL performance, yet existing NL2SQL systems largely assume that user queries are valid and answerable. As a result, models often generate executable SQL even for queries with flawed premises. We introduce premise critique ability in NL2SQL, namely the ability to recognize flawed queries and abstain from generating misleading SQL. To evaluate this capability, we propose PremiseSQL, a benchmark containing 1,800 flawed NL2SQL queries across four categories of premise failures, along with their 1,800 original queries. We further design an evaluation framework to measure intrinsic and prompt-induced premise-aware behavior across three prompting settings. Experiments on frontier LLMs show that current models are strongly premise-trusting by default and rarely critique flawed premises. Stronger critique-oriented prompting improves detection and abstention on flawed queries, but also increases false invalid judgments and suppresses SQL generation on originals. The code is available at https://github.com/vegeet/PremiseSQL.

papers.title: The Mission Market: Flying NASA's Vetted, Unflown Science
papers.abstract: Every year NASA validates more excellent science missions than it can afford to fly. Some of the most promising missions in astrophysics, heliophysics, and planetary science are judged selectable, yet remain grounded indefinitely. Mission Market is an advance market commitment that can fly lower cost missions without competing for federal appropriations. Funding comes primarily from the enormous capital now flowing into artificial intelligence (AI) companies that value generating frontier data for scientific foundation models and is also supplemented by traditional means such as philanthropy and patron-scientists.

papers.title: EMO: A Closed-Loop Test-Time Computation Framework via Alternating Context Optimization and Logits Steering
papers.abstract: Test-time context optimization adapts frozen language models through textual feedback, but ordinary conditional generation provides no separate control over how strongly to reinforce the distributional changes induced by a context update. We introduce EMO, a training-free framework inspired by expectation--maximization that alternates question-specific context estimation (E-step) and distribution refinement (M-step). The E-step revises a system context using textual gradients from an external judge without access to gold answers. The M-step contrasts next-token distributions under the revised and preceding contexts at a shared prefix to construct a confidence-constrained logit correction. Feedback on the steered response drives the next context update, coupling adaptation across rounds with intervention within each generation. Theoretically, we connect parameter and context optimization through a shared target-KL objective and additive logit representations, and derive the steering vector from context-induced logit displacements. Under context-improvement and faithful-steering assumptions, we prove a one-round decrease in target KL divergence for sufficiently small steering strength. Under greedy decoding across eight models and six benchmarks, EMO improves the zero-shot baseline in 39 of 40 aggregated settings, averaging $+9.10$ percentage points. With the same judge, it adds $+1.53$ points on average over context-only optimization (TextGrad), with consistent MMLU-Pro gains across models. At matched target-model generation budgets, accuracy advantages over best-of-$N$ are strongest on Llama, while oracle coverage is higher in most comparisons despite fewer candidates. The coverage--selection gap motivates allocating test-time computation jointly to candidate generation and verification.

papers.title: Gluing weak approximability along recollements
papers.abstract: We study whether weak approximability glues along recollements of triangulated categories that are compactly generated by a single object. This is applied to derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and prescribed support for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.

papers.title: The invariant cell number property for $\mathbb{E}_4$-rings
papers.abstract: For any non-zero $\mathbb{E}_4$-ring $R$, we prove that an $n$-fold direct sum of suspensions of $R$ cannot admit an exhaustive filtration by fewer than $n$ cells. We do this by showing that certain integral representations of the symmetric group lift to Schur functors on additively $\mathbb{E}_3$-monoidal $\infty$-categories. We then reduce the statement to a vanishing fact for rational Schur functors due to Deligne.

papers.title: Multi-sourced AI Tutor for Non-Native English Speaker Students
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non-native English speaker (NNES) students face in computing courses due to language barriers. To aid such students, we developed a general-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages (currently focused on Mandarin) and provide bilingual responses. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner. The tutor also provided high-quality translations for 76.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64.47% of them. Our findings underscore the potential of multi-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course.

papers.title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
papers.abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill makes mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, but what it damages has not been measured. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions in four MoE families on short-answer question answering. At half the experts the F1 loss is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but no longer answers briefly. The loss is made at a few tokens: the two chat-template tokens before the answer in Qwen3-30B-A3B, and the first 8-32 tokens, where the instruction sits, in DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Keeping them at full experts removes most of the F1 loss and about half and a fifth of the increase in answer NLL. Reduction changes the first-token sink statistics by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most a quarter of the loss. We then test placement on real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts. Putting them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while the same budget scattered in the documents is about 3 points worse in both prespecified primary tests of this comparison. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts.

papers.title: Frequency comb stability, bistability, and self-starting in normal dispersion microresonators
papers.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that it is possible to generate frequency combs in normal dispersion microresonators by taking advantage of fabricated mode coupling that induces a mode split. In particular, photonic crystal resonators periodically modulate the microresonator's width, which geometrically creates mode coupling. In contrast to frequency combs generated by microresonators in the anomalous dispersion regime, which are typically generated using bright solitons, the frequency combs generated by normal dispersion regime microresonators are dark pulses that are commonly referred to as dark solitons or platicons. In this work, we examine the linear stability of platicons in the pump-detuning and pump-power parameter space as the mode split strength and cavity dispersion is varied. Our work reveals a broad region of stability for platicons. Our work also reveals the existence of fingers at high power at whose boundaries a sharp transition occurs and inside of which platicon solutions are bistable. Finally, we investigate the overlap of the region where platicons are stable with the region where continuous waves are modulationally unstable, and it is possible for a platicon to self-start. Simulations show that platicons consistently self-start inside this region.

papers.title: Investigation of an X-class Flare and Quasi-Periodic Pulsations in NOAA AR 13842 using SDO, Aditya-L1 and Solar Orbiter
papers.abstract: We investigate an X9.0 class flare (SOL2024-10-03T12:08) and associated quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) in NOAA active region (AR) 13842 using observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), Aditya-L1 and Solar Orbiter (SO). To explore the role of magnetic configuration in the flare, we employ non-force-free-field extrapolation technique for reconstructing a sequence of the coronal magnetic field throughout the flare. The observations reveal the emergence of intricate flare brightenings and ribbons. QPPs are observed with periods of $\approx$ 2 and $\approx$ 6 minutes in EUV, $\approx$ 7 minutes in UV, and $\approx$ 1 minute in X-rays. The extrapolation documents the presence of a flux rope, a sheared arcade, and a hyperbolic flux tube (HFT) enveloping the rope and the arcade. The sequence of the extrapolation illustrates an increase in the twist of the rope as it ascends towards a torus-unstable region, thereby rendering the rope a viable candidate for eruption. The sheared arcade appears to generate electric current through its foot-point's motion, which explains the sigmoidal brightening observed at the flare onset. The motion also seems to drive the non-parallel field lines closer together, heightening gradient in the magnetic field beneath the rope. Consequently, recurrent magnetic reconnection is anticipated within the sheared arcade --- explaining the ascent of the rope with its twist increment. The formation of parallel flare ribbons is attributed to these reconnections. Furthermore, reconnection at the HFT is proposed to lead the remote and quasi-circular ribbons. Crucially, repeated reconnections inside the arcade as well as at the HFT are speculated to cause the QPPs.

papers.title: Cone Invariance and Homoclinic Standing Waves for Cooperative Finite-Range DNLS Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a constrained-power variational framework for positive homoclinic standing waves in one-dimensional discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equations with cooperative finite-range interactions. Starting from periodic lattices, we construct constrained energy maximizers and use the associated projected gradient flow to establish positive invariance of the cone of nonnegative, even, and unimodal profiles. A central result is that the monotone ordering of the interaction coefficients, \(a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots\ge a_M\ge0\), with \(a_1>0\), provides the structural condition ensuring preservation of this cone under finite-range coupling. Under a strict maximum condition above the linear spectral edge, we obtain a uniform frequency gap and period-independent exponential localization. These estimates provide the compactness required for the infinite-period limit and yield positive, even, unimodal, and exponentially localized homoclinic standing waves as strong \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\)-limits of periodic constrained maximizers. Numerical computations for several interaction ranges and cooperative kernels illustrate the effects of extended coupling on dispersion and localization and support the periodic-to-homoclinic convergence predicted by the analysis.

papers.title: CLUE: Uncovering Social Context for Pragmatic Understanding
papers.abstract: Understanding a conversation requires connecting what is said to the speakers' relationships, expectations, and earlier exchanges. Prior work shows that supplying relevant context can improve models' social judgments, but much of this information may already be present in the conversation. This motivates training models to discover the cues that matter and use them to support an interpretation. We propose CLUE, a two-stage training pipeline that combines supervised evidence reasoning with GRPO guided by Grounded Information Utilization ($\mathrm{IU}_{\mathrm{G}}$). This reward credits new, evidence-supported social inferences while accounting for reasoning effort. We train on a small set of conversational examples to assess effectiveness and generalization across tasks, languages, and genres. At inference time, the trained model reasons over the supplied interaction in a self-contained manner. Compared with base Qwen, CLUE achieves relative gains of 17.3% in-domain and 9.3% out-of-domain in average weighted F1, with higher F1 on four of five out-of-domain evaluations. These gains are accompanied by over 80% fewer reasoning tokens on average in both domains. Human evaluation further finds that CLUE more often grounds its explanations in specific conversational content, with closer alignment between its quoted evidence and human-selected context.

papers.title: X-ray point sources towards the giant radio lobes of Centaurus A
papers.abstract: Centaurus A (NGC 5128) is the nearest radio galaxy (d = 3.8 Mpc), so individual X-ray point sources can be resolved against its giant radio lobes. We test whether a compact X-ray source population over the lobes exceeds the expected field population, once the selection function, foreground stars and the cosmic X-ray background (CXB) are accounted for. From five Chandra/ACIS-I lobe pointings we build a 0.5-7 keV catalogue of 185 sources, with Bayesian hardness ratios, Gaia DR3 and AllWISE counterparts, and spectral fits to the eight brightest. The hardness-ratio distribution (median -0.17; 80% of sources below N_H = 10^22 cm^-2) is that of background AGN plus a few foreground stars. Above the flux at which half the footprint is covered, the good sample holds 83 sources, 9 of them foreground stars, against 101 expected background sources: 27% below the expectation (-1.5 sigma including a 15% normalisation uncertainty), with no excess. The 90% upper limit on a lobe-associated excess above 6.9x10^36 erg/s is N_lobe < 18, or < 38 for a conservative 30% normalisation uncertainty. With the usual resolved-source masking and CXB subtraction, no additional lobe-associated correction to diffuse-emission or inverse-Compton measurements is indicated.

papers.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
papers.abstract: The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics, and the embedding and unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods reuse a fixed lens or treat states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state as the model does. We argue that every hidden state has a native reference frame, induced by the layers that remain and adaptive to the context. Lexical reference frames approximate it in a model-native and context-aware way, reading a state through the remaining layers with a given number of rounds of attention between positions and a typical attention output for the rest, fitting nothing to the model's output. No lens with fixed directions per layer can reach a mean cosine with the native frame's lexical readouts above the square root of their coherence, 0.30 and 0.35 at mid-depth of SmolLM3-3B and OLMo3-7B. LexFrame[1], of order 1, reaches 0.97 and 0.97, and its readings are on average within 0.16 and 0.15 nats of the model's output. Its coefficient differences attribute predictions more faithfully than attribution patching, and its lexical basis steers predictions while sparing other tokens. On average, its readings settle on the model's top token over the final 0.82 and 0.81 of the layers, those of lenses over at most 0.11. These frames thus make every hidden state readable, attributable and steerable.

papers.title: Segal's semigroup, Virasoro structure, and Ward identities in Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory
papers.abstract: Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory (CILT for short) is a probabilistically constructed Conformal Field Theory (CFT), expected to have connections to minimal models, Coulomb gas integrals, and loop models. In this paper, we study the quantization of Segal's semigroup given by CILT. Each element $\mathbf T_f$ in the quantized semigroup corresponds to a conformal annulus: the unit disk $\mathbb D$ with $f(\mathbb D^\circ)$ removed, where $f:\mathbb D\to f(\mathbb D)\subset \mathbb D^\circ$ is a contracting biholomorphism. This semigroup encodes the local conformal structure of the CFT, in particular the Virasoro symmetry with central charge $<1$ for CILT. We first relate the quantized Segal's semigroup to Segal's amplitudes of annuli and recover the Virasoro generators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\geq0$) of CILT as generators of this semigroup. Compared to the real Liouville CFT, the main difficulty here is the absence of positivity, which we address through estimates for the imaginary Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos and non-self-adjoint operators. Using Segal's gluing axiom as in the real case, we differentiate the amplitude and use conformal covariance to derive the Ward identities in terms of all Virasoro operators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$). We also outline the parallel theory for Boundary CILT (BCILT), concerning Segal's semigroup of semiannuli. These results provide essential tools for the conformal bootstrap program of (B)CILT, boundary BPZ equations, boundary structure constants, and the global construction of conformal blocks.

papers.title: Double covers of tori for p=2 and genuine functions
papers.abstract: In his work on $L$-embeddings and double covers of tori over local fields, Kaletha associates to a maximal torus $S$ in a connected reductive group a canonical double cover $S(F)_{\pm}$ and introduces a genuine sign function $a_S$ associated to a genuine character of $S(F)_{\pm}$. We give two constructions of this genuine sign function over a non-archimedean local field, including residual characteristic $2$. The first uses rootwise lifts to the double cover; the second, in characteristic zero, uses the exponential map. Under explicit ramification conditions, both constructions yield genuine sign functions which, in odd residual characteristic, agree with his construction. We also illustrate the case of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$. A brief announcement of the first construction appears in Appendix D of that work.

papers.title: Efficient KV Cache Migration for Geo-Distributed LLM Inference in Collaborative Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown exceptional capabilities but rely heavily on centralized cloud GPU clusters, leading to high bandwidth costs, latency, and privacy issues.
